metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 06/12/2025] An I.A.No.III filed by the Jdr is dismissed. The Memo filed by the Dhr is hereby allowed and E.P is closed as fully satisfied.
metadata.Order Procedural History: The learned counsel for the Dhr filed memo stating that, the Dhr has taken possession of the suit property through court process. EP is fully satisfied. Hence, E.P may be closed. 2. The learned counsel for the Jdr filed I.A.No.II Under order 21 Rule 58 r/w. 151 of CPC and U/s.6 of Specific Relief Act seeking for restoration of his possession over suit property and further stated that he has legally disposed from the suit property. 3. Heard both sides. 4. The following points that arise for my consideration: :- Whether there is sufficient grounds for allow the I.A.No.III.? :-What Order ? 5. By considering the memo and I.A, and hearing of the parties, my answer for the above point is as under: :- In the Negative, :- As per final order 2
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: for the following:- 7. :- The learned Dhr submitted that in order to cause delay the present application is filed by the Jdr. The Jdr is very well aware about the pending of this E.P. He ha kept quite until completion of the process of execution of the warrant, at the fag end of the case, he has filed false application. Hence, prays to reject the application. 8. The learned counsel for the Jdr submitted that after Jdr challenged the Judgment and order passed by this court in before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA.No.410/2023, the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka issued notice to Dhr. The Dhr has also appeared before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in the said appeal. The Dhr has failed to comply the provision of order 21 Rule 34 (2) of CPC. He has not produced any E.C while executing of the sale deed. The Jdr has prima-facie case. Hence, 3 prays to allow the application and stay the proceedings and handover the possession in favour of the Jdr. 9. I have carefully perused the entire material on record. The Dhr has filed this Execution petition on 02.03.2023 and issued notice to the Jdr through paper publication. Notice to Jdr is served. In spite of that he has failed to appear before this court. Sale deed executed in favour of the Dhr through process. Thereafter, issued possession deliver warrant which was duly executed. In this case the Court Ameen has submitted his report, mahazar and possession receipt. The very object of the execution petition is already served. 10. Jdr not submitted regarding whether the execution of the Judgment and order passed by this court in is stayed by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA.No. 410/2023. By 4 considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion, present application is filed to defeat the very object of the speedy disposal of the case and to deny, obstruct the fruits of the decree. Therefore, I am of the opinion that there is no grounds to allow the I.A.No.III. Hence, point No.1 is answered in the Negative. 11. P oint No.3 :- In view of my findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following:

hearings.judge: CCH64 LXIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Learned counsel for DHR filed IA.No.II U/o 26 rule 9 of CPC, seeking for appointment of court commissioner for the purpose perform ministerial act of this court. Heard. The learned counel for DHR urged that, in this case this court granted relief of specific performance of contract by passing judgment and decree in O.S.No.4555/2020 dated 02.07.2022. As per the said judgment and decree the JDR is requires to execute sale deed in favour of DHR petitioner within 3 months from the date judgment. The JDR fails to execute sale deed by receiving remaining balance sale consideration. Hence, prays for appointment of court commissioner for the purpose of execution of sale deed on behalf of JDR. I have perused the IA.No.I, petition and decree. In O.S.No.4555/2020 this court decreed the suit of the plaintiff and directed to defendant execute the sale deed by receiving sale consideration within 3 months from 02.07.2022. There is no record to show that, the judgement passed by this court is setaside or stayed by competant court of law. It is just and proper to appointment of court commissioner for performing minsterial act on behalf of this court. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:- ORDER IA.No.II filed U/o 26 rule 9 of CPC is hereby consider as filed U/o 26 rule 10-B of CPC and hereby allowed. One Advocate of Advocate’s Bar Bengaluru is appointed as court commissioner. The learned counsel for DHR filed memo with draft sale deed. Call on by 08.08.2024.

metadata.Case Title: H L L LIFECARE LIMITED vs M/S SUPER THREADS INDIA
metadata.Court Name: PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Court Room & Judge: 18-CCH16 XVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 30/09/2024] 10 Ex.P.No.16/2023 District Court Hukkeri without having any jurisdiction, on an application filed u/Sec.11 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act appointed an arbitrator. The Hon'ble High Court of Trivandrum is having jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute between the parties after two years of filing the suit bearing . The respondents in the year 2017 filed I.A. u/Sec.11 of the Act stating that since there is an arbitration clause in the purchase order that an arbitrator be appointed. Inspite of issuance of reply, the decree holder has failed to furnish required documents i.e. entire order sheet, judgment, decree in and also entire order sheet maintained by the arbitrator. The learned counsel for the judgment debtor has relied upon rulings reported in:- (1) 2019 SCCOnline KAR 276 (Para No.8 and 9), in the case of Mohammed Shafi and another V/s. Mohammed Ashapak Hussain. (2) 1972 (2) SCC 662 (Headnote B; Para 3) in the case of Sunder Dass V/s. Ram Prakash.
metadata.Order Procedural History: 6 Ex.P.No.16/2023 ORDERS The learned counsel for JDR has filed preliminary objections contending that this Court has no any jurisdiction to entertain this petition as the District Court in Hukkeri without having any jurisdiction, passed an order on an application filed u/Sec.11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. For brevity (here in after referred to as Act) and appointed an arbitrator. As per Sec.11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, application can be filed only before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka. The application is not maintainable before a District Judge. In view of the same, the arbitrator appointed has lacked inherent jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute between the parties and pass any award. Hence, the award passed by the arbitrator is a nullity in law and there can be no enforcement of any award passed by the arbitrator in the present case. Any enforcement of this award that is patently illegal would be against public order and justice. The decree holder had fraudulently approached the Hukkeri District Court and filed in spite of being aware that 7 Ex.P.No.16/2023 the respondent was present in Bengaluru and no cause of action has arisen in Hukkeri District. As per arbitration clause, the Courts of Trivandrum had jurisdiction of power, authority to adjudicate any disputes between the parties after two years of filing the suit bearing . hearings.business_text: Show cause notice to the Spl. Thasildhar has been duly served, under which this court had sought the explanation to the salary drawing officer of the JDR herein for not attaching the salary of the JDR to satisfy the decree. The service of the show cause notice to the garnishee of the JDR has been reported to this court. Thus Spl. Thasildhar Yelahanka Taluk has fails to send his explanation and fails to appear before this court, thus this court felt, it is proper to call the Spl. Thasildhar to be present before this court. Accordingly ordered to issue notice to the Spl. Thasildhar Yelahanka Taluk Yelahanka, Bangalore to place his physicall appearance before this court on next date of hearing without fail. In this case, despite issuance of S/A/W to the garnishee of the JDR the same has not been carried out by the garnishee and despite service of show cause notice the garnishee remained absent. If that aspect is considered the garnishee may be hand in glow of the JDR, with intend to frustrate the decree of this court. Thus this court felt it is proper to order for issue arrest notice to the JDR. Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on IA.No. 2. As the DHR made out the grounds that it is the JDR and his garnishee with intend to frustrate the decree are evading the process of this court, thus IA.No. 2 filed by the DHR is hereby allowed, ordered to issue arrest notice against the JDR, if the DHR pays the PF in the office. hearings.business_text: Statement of objection have been filed by JDR advocate. As per statement of objection cheque bearing no. 230962 dated 29.03.2014 of Rs.1,84,00,000/- pertaining to survey no. 215 of Bheemanakuppe Village has been numbered as LAC 57/2014 and the same day the JDR has sent another cheque bearing no.230963 dated 29.03.2014 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- pertaining to survey no. 205 of Bheemanakuppe Village, which was numbered as LAC 64/2014. It is stated that the office while registering the above cases with regard to amount in LAC 64/2014 have deposited the amount of Rs.1,84,00,000/- instead of Rs. 1,18,00,000/- and vice versa. The office while depositing the amount in LAC 57/2014 have deposited a sum of Rs.1,18,00,000/- instead of Rs.1,84,00,000/-. On perusal of both the records in LAC 57/2014 and 64/2014 it is seen that with regard to LAC 64/2014 the BDA has sent letter dated 09.04.2014 along with cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- but the office has taken cheque no. 230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/-. On perusal of record in LAC 57/2014 it is seen that BDA has sent letter No.885/09-10 cheque no. 230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/- but the office has taken cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/-. There is mistake committed by the office in taking the cheques in LAC 57/2014 and LAC 64/2014. Hence, the amount deposited in respect of cheque no.230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/- has to be transferred to LAC 57/2014 and the amount deposited in respect of cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- has to be transferred to LAC 64/2014. Copy of this order to be entered in LAC 57/2014 and LAC 64/2014 . Call on 22-08-2023.

Upon perusal of order sheet, it is noticed that, on the earlier dates of hearing, the counsel for DHR was directed to take steps against JDR No.1 and 2 for the issuance of cause notices. Despite providing multiple opportunities, the DHR has failed to take proper steps against Jdr No.1 for taking steps to issue cause notices in order to effectively execute the decree. In view of the judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs & Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani & Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640- 3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025 and in compliance of the circular No.2/2025 dated 01.04.2025 issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka mandating the disposal of execution petitions within 6 months, this Court is duty bound to prevent undue pendency of the execution petitions. Since the DHR has not diligently pursued the execution and no purpose would be served in keeping the petition pending further, the execution petition deserves to be disposed of. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification. 22.08.2026 XXXIV ACC & SJ., & Spl. Judge, (NDPS), Bengaluru. (CCH-35)

judicial_order.procedural_history: Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. Upon perusal of order sheet, it is noticed that, on the earlier dates of hearing, the counsel for DHR was directed to take steps against JDR No.1 and 2 for the issuance of cause notices. Despite providing multiple opportunities, the DHR has failed to take proper steps against Jdr No.1 for taking steps to issue cause notices in order to effectively execute the decree. In view of the judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs & Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani & Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640- 3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025 and in compliance of the circular No.2/2025 dated 01.04.2025 issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka mandating the disposal of execution petitions within 6 months, this Court is duty bound to prevent undue pendency of the execution petitions. Since the DHR has not diligently pursued the execution and no purpose would be served in keeping the petition pending further, the execution petition deserves to be disposed of. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification. 22.08.2026 XXXIV ACC & SJ., & Spl. Judge, (NDPS), Bengaluru. (CCH-35)

hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The Delivery warrant issued against the JDR returned unexecuted as kept locked and also reported that the JDR has inducted the tenants in the petition schedule property. As the decree for possession, the tenants under the possession of the JDR are bound by the decree. Thus this court felt they are not necessary party before this court to issue notice to them. Considering the same, this court felt proper to re-issue Delivery warrant with directions to break open the lock of the petition schedule property. The DHR files IA.No.2 u/O 21 R 35 of CPC by seeking an order to break open the locks of the petition schedule properties and to deliver the vacant possession in favor of the DHR herein. As the JDR is obstructing the executing the Delivery warrant by kept locking the petition schedule property and appears to be inducted some 3rd party into the petition schedule property to delay the execution proceedings. Thus IA.No.2 filed by the DHR is hereby allowed. Ordered to issue Delivery warrant with directions to the bailiff to break open the lock of the petition schedule property and demolish the building stands on the petition schedule property with the assistance of the men and material of the DHR and deliver the vacant petition schedule property in favour of the DHR. Directed the DHR to extend with sufficient men and material to demolish the building found on the petition schedule property. And also directed the jurisdictional Hebbal police to extend the police protection to the officer of this court to execute the Delivery warrant to deliver the vacant possession of the petition schedule property in favor of the DHR herein. Call on 09.11.2023.

hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Sri LB files vakalath for JDR and files IA.No. 1 u/o 21 R 35 of CPC by seeking an order to issue delivery warrant to deliver the vacant possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the existed structure with the police protections. In this case, the DHR has got the decree for possession wherein, directed the JDR herein to deliver the vacant possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the building existed therein within 90 days from the date of Judgment. The Judgment dt 27.01.2022 and the JDR submitted the against the Judgment and decree of this cour the JDR has not preferred an appeal, thus this court felt as the JDR is fails to comply the Judgment and Decree, thus it is proper to deliver the vacant possession of the petition schedule property in favour of DHR herein by executing the delivery warrant. Accordingly IA.No. 1 is hereby allowed, delivery warrant is been issued to deliver the petition schedule property in favour of the DHR herein and permitted the bailiff of this court to take sufficient assistance to demolish the building existed on petition schedule property. Thus directed the DHR to extend his all assistance by providing men and machinery to carryout the demolition work and liberty is being given to the DHR to file calculation memo on the expenditure made for the demolition to recover from the JDR. To avoid the obstruction if any to come in the way of bailiff to execute the warrant to deliver the possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the structure therein it is proper to extend police security. Thus directed the police inspector attached to the Jurisdiction Hebbal Police station to extend the police protections to the officer of this court to execute the warrant as and when he approaches the police station by providing sufficient men. For await report. Call on 30.08.2023

hearings.business_text: Passed over on submission of the counsel for DHR. Again called at 3-20 pm. The DHR counsel submits that I.A.No.3 is not pressing. Hence, I.A.No.3 is dismissed as not pressed. The DHR counsel is present. She filed I.A.No.4 under Order XXI Rule 43 of CPC for attachment of movable property as per the inventory made by the bailiff and I.A.No.5 under Order XXI Rule 64 of CPC for sale of movable properties by public action. Heard the counsel for DHR on I.A.No.4 and 5. Perused the record. The DHR has filed EP for execution of decree in OS.No.2524/2022 for delivery warrant and also for recovery of arrears of rent. As per the report of bailiff dated 07/03/2023, the possession of the schedule premises has been delivered to the DHR. He also made inventory that the movables of the JDR valuing of Rs.16,100/- are handed over to the DHR custody. The DHR has filed applications for attachment and sale of movables of the JDR and adjust the sale proceeds towards claim amount. In view of reasons, I.A.No.4 and 5 are allowed, the movable properties of the JDR as per the inventory of the bailiff are attached and ordered to be sold in public action. Issue sale proclamation of movables of the JDR, the spot sale is fixed by giving 07 days time from the date on which the copy of the proclamation has been affixed on the Court house, as required under Order XXI Rule 68 of CPC. Accordingly, the spot sale is on 30/03/2023. For Court sale/final bid, by 06/04/2023.

In single application, two reliefs are claim and to file proper application for sale of the property, by 13/03/2023.

hearings.business_text: The case is taken on board as per the advanced application filed by the counsel for the DHR. The counsel for DHR Miss.AS, is present. She submits that the bailiff has returned delivery warrant seeking police help. The delivery warrant issued by the Court on 21/01/2023 as returned unexecuted as schedule premises has been locked. The bailiff in his report along with mahazar conducted as prays for to break open the lock and reissue warrant. Whereas, the counsel for DHR has filed application to break open the lock with police assistance. Heard, in view of report of bailiff, reissue delivery warrant with a direction to break open the lock of the premises and with assistance of jurisdiction police if required and execute warrant by making inventory and mahazar. Call on 07/03/2023.

hearings.business_text: Heard the counsel for Dhr. In the instant case, Jdr.No.1 and 4 are placed exparte. Though sufficient time has been given Jdr.No.2 has not filed objection. Perused the judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has set-aside the judgment and decree passed by this court in O.S.2871/2003 and decreed the suit in favor of the plaintiffs. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has further held that judgment and decree passed in O.S.10476/1988 and in R.F.A.No.44/1996 are not binding on the plaintiffs and consequently declared the plaintiffs as the absolute owners of the suit schedule property and directed the legal representative of defendants to hand the vacant possession of the petitioin schedule property. In view of judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A. No.219/2014, I feel it is necessary to issue delivery warrant against the legal representatives of defendant/Jdrs herein. Further, as per office note, no stay or appeal pending against judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. Hence, issue delivery warrant against Jdrs to hand over the vacant possession of the petition schedule property to the Dhr. R/by 22.09.2023.

hearings.business_text: DHR has filed this execution petition against the JDR for decreetal amount of Rs.44150 including interest from 15.01.2022 till 15.01.2023 at the rate of 12 percent p.a of Rs57395 The learned counsel for the JDR submitted that, as per the decree he has paid the entire amount and he is not liable to pay any interest. On going through the materials placed before me, this petition is filed against the judgment passed by the trial court in C.C.No.6126-2014 and judgment passed by this Court in Crl.A.No.542-2015 and order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka in Crl.R.P.No.889-2016 C/W 770-2016 before lok adalath. On going through the said order of the Hon\\\''ble High Court of Karnataka the respondent Sangana Gouda B Patil i.e the JDR herein undertook to pay the sum of Rs.8,25,000 to the present DHR and in turn the present DHR is permitted to withdraw an amount of Rs.3,83,50- deposited before the Trial Court and balance amount of Rs.4,41,500 is to be paid by the present JDR to the present DHR within 6 months from the date of the said order. On going through the order sheet the JDR has filed D.D. for Rs.2,00,000 on 21.12.2023 and again on 25.01.2024 he has handed over 2 D.Ds for an amount of Rs.1,00,000 and Rs.41,500 to the counsel for the DHR. Again on 13.03.2024 JDR filed D.D for Rs.1,00,00-. In total JDR has paid 4,41,500. Hence, it is clear that the JDR has already paid Rs.4,41,500 as ordered by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka and this petition is filed for collecting interest at the rate of 12percent p.a, which nowhere finds place in the order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka and it has not discussed regarding the interest.In the circumstances, without any speaking order DHR is not entitled to receive 12 percent interest on the principal amount. As on now, the JDR has paid the entire decreetal amount as per the order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka. Hence, to report closure of execution petition by 08.08.2024.

metadata.Order Procedural History: Ex. 264/2023 This execution petition is filed by the Decree Holder to enforce the decree passed in as per the Judgment dated 17/6/2015 and the decree dated 17/6/2015. As per the said judgment and decree, the Judgment Debtor is directed to execute the sale deed in favour of the plaintiffs in respect of suit schedule property by receiving balance sale consideration of Rs.50,000/- and put the Ex. 264/2023 Decree holder / plaintiffs in possession of the same. If the Judgment Debtor / defendant failed to execute the sale deed, the decree holder / plaintiffs can get the sale deed through court by depositing the balance consideration of Rs.50,000/- in the court and take possession of the suit schedule property. As per the petition averment, the Judgment Debtor has challenged the aforesaid Judgment before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA No.1160/2015 and there is no stay order granted in the said RFA by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, inspite of that the Judgment Debtor has not executed the sale deed. Hence this execution petition is filed by the Decree Holder. As the Judgment Debtor failed to execute the sale deed, it is just and necessary to appoint the Court Commissioner to execute the sale deed in respect of the decreed property. Hence the following: ORDERS The Senior Sheristedar of this court namely Smt.Vijaya Dasarahalli has been appointed as a Court Commissioner to execute the sale deed in favour of Decree Holder through SPA holder of Decree Holder. The Commissioner’s fee is tentatively fixed at Rs.5,000/-. Commissioner Report by 18/11/2023. (PADMA PRASAD) XVIII Additional City Civil Judge, Bengaluru.

hearings.judge: CCH2 I ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: This is a petition filed by the DHR to give direction to the jurisdictional police to give sufficient protection to the DHR The office raised objection regarding limitation. From the judgment or decree discloses that, the DHR got the partition and also the court held that the Plaintiff is entitled for permanent injunction and also restrained the defendant from dispossessing the Plaintiff from the Suit Schedule property. The Learned advocate for the DHR has argued that to enforce the DHR in permanent injunction suit limitation will not applicable. Hence, he requested to over rule the office objections. To substantiate his argument he is relied upon the judgment of the Hon\''ble Orissa High Court passed in Chakaradara patil (dead by LRS) Vs Geetha Bhava. I have gone through the judgment of the Orissa Hon\''ble High Court where in the Hon\''ble High Court held that as per the provision to article 136 of limitation act there is no limitation for execution of a decree for permanent injunction. Therefore the execution case in question cannot be said to be barred by law of limitation. This ruling is applicable to the case of the DHR since this court granted the injunction against the defendant and the DHR can enforce the decree when JDR violated the court order. Accordingly, office objection regarding the limitation is overruled. Issue notice to JDR, if PF is paid. Call on 20.06.2023.

hearings.business_text: Heard both side on IA.No.1. This IA is filed by the DHR under Order VI Rule 17 of the CPC r/w Sec.151 of the CPC to delete existing suit schedule property and insert the property bearing No.484 as per decree. It is stated by the DHR that due to clerical error the schedule property is wrongly mentioned. JDR filed objection stating that the present schedule property mentioned in the EP is not related OS.6668/2014 and application is filed at belated stage. As per the decree passed in OS.6668/2014 the suit property is site No.484 situated at Mallathhalli Village but in Execution Petition the suit property is shown as the land bearing Sy.No.33 new Sy.No.93 of Mallasandra Village. So, it appears that due to clerical error the said mistake is occured in the petition. Hence, it can be corrected. This EP is filed to execute the decree in OS.6668/2014. Hence, the suit property is said suit has to be mentioned as suit property in this EP. Hence, IA.No.1 is allowed. DHR is permitted to amend the schedule of the EP. For amendment and amended petition. Call on 17-10-2025.

metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 09/12/2023] 09-12-2023 EX 316/2023 Lok-adalath Bench No.123/2023. Case called before lok-adalath. Decree holder and Ld. Counsel present. With due intervention of conciliators, matter settled. Decree Holder filed memo reporting full and final settlement and payment of decreetal amount by the judgment debtor and prays to close the Execution petition. Being satisfied that the settlement is voluntary and lawful, this Lok- Adalath bench proceed to pass the following : ORDER Memo filed by decree holder is allowed. Consequently, this Execution petition is closed as fully satisfied. (KALPANA M.S.) ADV CONCILIATOR JUDICIAL CONCILIATOR

metadata.Case Title: SRINIVAS vs MUNIRAJU V
metadata.Court Name: PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Court Room & Judge: 26-CCH23 XXV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 14/10/2025] Memo dated 14.09.2023 filed by the JDR is hereby allowed and EP is dismissed as fully satisfied. Under the circumstances, parties to the petition shall bear their own costs. (14.10.2025) XXV Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bangalore
metadata.Order Procedural History: Ex.No.321/2023 ORDERS ON MEMO DATED 14.09.2023 AND AFFIDAVIT OF JDR V. MUNIRAJU In fact, the Decree Holders have filed the petition under Order XXI Rule 11 of CPC for the execution of Judgment and Decree drawn on O.S. No. 5682/2016. A perusal of compromise petition filed in O.S. No.5682/2016 under Order XXIII Rule 3 of CPC would show that, the defendant had agreed to take possession of property bearing site No.46 formed in Sy. No.26 from mortgagee's and hand over the same to the plaintiffs along with original documents. Now, JDR would submit that in pursuance with compromise so arrived in O.S. No.5682/2016, he had handed over possession of the property bearing No.46 along with original documents to the plaintiffs. Hence, he requested the court to dismiss the petition as fully satisfied. In fact, Memo dated 14.09.2023 is accompanied with a joint memo. This memo is signed by Decree Holder as well as their counsels. As per this Memo, JDR had handed over physical possession of the premises along with original documents to the Decree Holders. The contents of joint Memo is not at all denied by the Decree Holders. In addition to it, it is not their contention Ex.No.321/2023 that joint Memo does not bear their signatures and signature of their counsel. Now objection is filed by the Decree Holder to the Memo to the effect that they admit the Memo in part however original documents are not handed over by the JDR. This objection has no legs to stand because joint Memo signed by Decree Holders and their counsel would clearly indicate that Decree Holders have not only taken possession of the schedule property but also original documents. Hence, objection so filed by the Decree Holder does not merit for consideration. Since because, joint memo speaks about delivery of vacant possession of suit schedule premises along with original documents, there is nothing to be executed against the JDR. In the Execution Petition, Decree Holders have claimed Rs.6,50,000/- payable to the mortgagors. A perusal of compromise petition filed in O.S. No.5682/2016 would show that it is for the plaintiffs to pay a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- to the defendants out of Rs.6,50,000/- and it is for the defendant to pay remaining balance of Rs.3,50,000/- to the mortgagors. Now, it is shown to the satisfaction of the court that plaintiffs/ Decree Holders have already taken possession of the property and original documents also. Therefore, payment of a sum of Rs.6,50,000/- is between the JDR and Mortgagors. The Decree Holders cannot claim this amount.
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: Ex.No.321/2023 In addition to the above, JDR has sworn to an affidavit. The averments made in affidavit is in tune with joint Memo so filed containing signatures of Decree Holders and their counsel. In view of the above, Memo dated 14.09.2023 is deserves to be allowed by rejecting objection of the Decree Holders dated 27.06.2025. Therefore, the following:

metadata.Order Procedural History: Ex.No.335 / 2023 03.07.2024: ORDER ON I.A.NO.4 1. This application is filed by Decree Holder under Order 21 Rule 95 r/w Section 151 of CPC seeking this Court to direct the Judgment Debtor to vacate the schedule property and deliver the vacant physical possession of the schedule property to the Auction Purchaser – Decree Holder. 2. It is contended by the Applicant – Decree Holder – Auction Purchaser that he had filed a suit in as against the Judgment Debtor by name M.V. Srinivas seeking relief of Specific Performance of Agreement and that alternatively to refund the earnest money with interest at the rate of 18% p.a., and that this Court had alternatively decreed the said suit of the Plaintiff for refund of earnest money with interest at the rate of 18% p.a. But the Defendant – Judgment Debtor is said to have failed to make any payment of such on 03.02.2023, this Court had ordered an attachment of schedule property belonging to Judgment Debtor and that on 20.02.2023, the schedule property so attached was also proclaimed for sale by way of substituted service i.e., beating of Tom-Tom and in pursuance of the Ex.No.335 / 2023 said sale of proclamation on 24.05.2023, the date was scheduled for spot sale, but not of the bidders participated in the said Auction Sale. 2.2 Further it is also contended that the Decree Holder is said to have made an application before this Court and sought permission to participate in the bid i.e., Auction Sale and accordingly, the application was allowed and the Decree Holder was permitted to participate in the Auction Sale that was conducted on 16.01.2024 and he was declared as highest bidder and that the sale certificate was also issued in favour of Decree Holder as on 17.02.2024 and that in pursuance of the sale certificate, the Decree Holder has approached this Court seeking for vacant possession of the schedule property and in this regard, the Decree Holder has sought for issuance of notice to the Judgment Debtor to deliver the vacant possession of the schedule property. 3. Along with the said application, the Decree Holder has also furnished the certificate issued by this Court towards Auction Sale Certificate and also in the said certificate, the Decree Holder is said to have paid a sum of Rs.2,21,250/- and that as contended by Decree Holder, the sale proclamation is ordered and accordingly, a specific order is also passed with regard to the application (I.A.No.3) filed by this Decree Holder under Order 21 Rule 72 r/w Section 151 of CPC as 2
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: Ex.No.335 / 2023 on 15.11.2023, seeking permission to participate in the Auction Sale and further in presence of Decree Holder and Judgment Debtor, the Decree Holder is declared as the successful highest auction bidder, for a sum of Rs.44,25,000/- and that the order of set off the Decree Holder has agreed to purchase the schedule property for a sum of Rs.44,25,000/- and further the Judgment Debtor was given an opportunity to deposit the decreetal amount within a period of limitation, so that he could retain the property. But subsequently, no alteration is made by Judgment Debtor. Accordingly, the Decree Holder was declared as per the earlier order the highest bidder and set off the decreetal amount of Rs.45,03,145/- against the purchase money, sale certificate was issued. Accordingly, in pursuance of the same, the Decree Holder has approached this Court by way of this application seeking vacant possession of the attached property i.e., schedule property. 4. Having perused the same, the Decree Holder has made out grounds for issuance of delivery notice to the Judgment Debtor to deliver the vacant possession of the schedule property. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following: 3 Ex.No.335 / 2023 ORDER I.A.No.4 filed by Decree Holder under Order 21 Rule 95 r/w Section 151 of CPC is hereby allowed. Accordingly, since the decree of this Court is dated 09.11.2022, which is within two years from the date of the decree, issue delivery warrant as against Judgment Debtor in respect of the schedule property to hand over the vacant possession of the schedule property. (Dictated to the Stenographer Grade – I, transcribed and typed by him, corrected, printout taken, signed and then pronounced by me in the open Court on this the 3rd day of July, 2024) (A.M. NALINI KUMARI) XIV Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City. 4 Ex.No.335 / 2023 5

metadata.Order Judicial Findings: Ex.No.567/2023 decree in . The present petitioner is the objector in the said petition and he filed IA No.XXI Rule 58 R/w Section 151 of CPC claiming against the attachment of the immovable property and to release the property from the attachment wherein the said application was rejected by this Court. Thereafter, the objector filed Writ Petition Nos.6235-6236/2018 before the Hon’ble High Court to quash the order passed by this Court. The said writ petition was disposed in terms of compromise memo dated 20.01.2020. In pursuance of the said orders, the objector filed memo to withdraw the petition, which was allowed by this Court with liberty to file fresh execution petition. Subsequently, the objector has filed this execution petition seeking his claim of Rs.30,08,875/- against the Judgment- Debtor. Hence, the petition. 3. On the otherhand, the JDr has filed objection statement and contended that the petition is not maintainable and Decree-holder has no locus standi to file this petition against the JDr since there was no decree 3 Ex.No.567/2023 passed against this JDr in .2008. Further the petition is time barred and the decree is said to have been obtained by original Decree-holder, M/s.Reyami Interiors Pvt. Ltd. Therefore, he is not entitled for any sum payable under the said petition. The Decree-holder and JDr have no connection with each other in any of the suit or in and therefore, the present petition is misconceived. Further, the Ex.No.2099/2011 was dismissed by this Court and therefore, question of filing this petition is not allowed and the same is hit by proviso 11 of CPC. Further submits that, the JDr is not a party to the alleged compromise petition in W.P.No.6235- 6236/2018 and therefore, Decree-holder cannot claim against the JDr. Hence, prays to dismiss the petition. 4. Heard the learned counsel for both the parties on the applications and perused the records. 5. metadata.Order Procedural History: 1 Ex.No.580/2023 THE COURT OF V ADDITIONAL CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE AT BENGALURU Dated this the 9th day of January 2026 Present : SRI.VEDAMOORTHY B.S., B.A.(L)., LL.B., XXXI Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru (CCH-14) C/c V Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru (CCH-13) Ex.No.580/2023 DECREE HOLDER : Official Liquidator of M/s Karnataka Infrastructures Pvt. Ltd. V/s JUDGMENT DEBTORS : Naresh Sachdev & others. i. Provision under which the application is filed Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure R/w Article 136 of the Limitation Act, R/w Section 151 of the Code of the Civil Procedure. ii. Relief sought for To reject the Execution Petition. iii. The date on which the application is filed 14.08.2023 iv. Number of the application I.A.No.I v. The date on which the objections are filed by different opponents Not filed. vi. The date on which the orders were passed on the said application 09.01.2026 2 Ex.No.580/2023 ORDERS ON I.A.No.I The judgment debtor No.14 has filed I.A.No.I under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure R/w Article 136 of the Limitation Act R/w Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking an order to reject the Execution Petition as it is barred by limitation. 2. In support of I.A.No.I, the learned Counsel for judgment debtor No.14 has filed his Memorandum of Facts. 3. The decree holder has not filed objection to I.A.No.I. 4. Heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for judgment debtor No.14 on I.A.No.I. The learned Counsel for the decree holder has submitted that his arguments on I.A.No.I is may be taken as heard. The learned Counsel for judgment debtor No.14 has relied the following judgments :- i. The judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the case between Krishna Reddy, Since deceased by his LRs V/s The
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: 3 Ex.No.580/2023 Special Additional LAO, Bangalore Development Authority & another (ILR 2013 KAR 5353). ii. The judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case between Damodaran Pillai & others V/s South Indian Bank Ltd. [(2005) 7 SCC 300]. iii. The order of the National Company Law Tribunal, Kolkata Bench (Court-I) in the case between Machino Transport Pvt. Ltd. V/s Machino Finance Pvt. Ltd. (IAR (CA) No.213/KB/2023). iv. The judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Madra in the case between S.Suresh Kumar, Proprietor of Rolex Electro Cab V/s Prakash Chand Jain, Proprietor of Sir Mahaveer Suppliers (2021 SCC OnLine Mad 17164). 5. Perused the materials available on record. 6. The following point that has been arisen for my consideration: Whether the Execution Petition is barred by limitation ? If so, what order? 4 Ex.No.580/2023 7. My answer to the above point is in the Affirmative for the following: 8. This petition is filed by the decree holder under Order XXI Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure to execute the order dated 06.07.2006 passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Company Application No.1268/1992 in Company Petition No.11/1986. As per Section 433 of the Companies Act, 2013, the provision of Limitation Act shall, as far as may be, apply to proceedings or appeals before the Tribunal or the Appellate Tribunal, as the case may be. The decree holder filed this petition in view of Section 364 of the Companies Act, 1956 contending that the order of the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka may be enforced in the same manner as decree made by the civil Court in suit pending therein. Under Article 136 of the Limitation Act, the period of limitation for execution of any decree or order of any civil Court is 12 years when the decree or order become enforceable. In the present case on hand, the order under execution is enforceable on the date when the order 5 Ex.No.580/2023 in Company Application No.1268/1992 in Company Petition No.11/1986 was passed on 06.07.2006. The present petition is filed on 23.02.2023. Since the present petition is not filed within 12 years from the date of the order which became enforceable, the petition is barred by limitation. In the judgments and the orders relied by the learned Counsel for judgment debtor No.14, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and the Hon'ble High Court of Madras referred above held that the period of limitation cannot be condoned in the execution proceedings. For the above reasons, I answer the above point in the Affirmative. In the result, I proceed to pass the following : ORDERS I.A.No.I filed by judgment debtor No.14 under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure R/w Article 136 of the Limitation Act R/w Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking is hereby allowed.

If so, what order? 4 Ex.No.580/2023 7. My answer to the above point is in the Affirmative for the following: 8. This petition is filed by the decree holder under Order XXI Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure to execute the order dated 06.07.2006 passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Company Application No.1268/1992 in Company Petition No.11/1986. As per Section 433 of the Companies Act, 2013, the provision of Limitation Act shall, as far as may be, apply to proceedings or appeals before the Tribunal or the Appellate Tribunal, as the case may be. The decree holder filed this petition in view of Section 364 of the Companies Act, 1956 contending that the order of the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka may be enforced in the same manner as decree made by the civil Court in suit pending therein. Under Article 136 of the Limitation Act, the period of limitation for execution of any decree or order of any civil Court is 12 years when the decree or order become enforceable. In the present case on hand, the order under execution is enforceable on the date when the order 5 Ex.No.580/2023 in Company Application No.1268/1992 in Company Petition No.11/1986 was passed on 06.07.2006. The present petition is filed on 23.02.2023. Since the present petition is not filed within 12 years from the date of the order which became enforceable, the petition is barred by limitation. In the judgments and the orders relied by the learned Counsel for judgment debtor No.14, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and the Hon'ble High Court of Madras referred above held that the period of limitation cannot be condoned in the execution proceedings. For the above reasons, I answer the above point in the Affirmative. In the result, I proceed to pass the following : ORDERS I.A.No.I filed by judgment debtor No.14 under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure R/w Article 136 of the Limitation Act R/w Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking is hereby allowed.

Now, the learned counsel for DHR is present and filed process memo seeking cause notice to JDR to the cause title address. hearings.business_text: Dhr is present. Jdr is present. As could be seen from the record it appears that the Jdr has filed this execution petition to execute the Judgment and Decree passed by this Court in O.S.No.978/2022. As per the said decree the Jdr is directed to vacate the schedule property by hand over the vacant possession to the plaintiff and also pay arrears rent of Rs.2,51,790/- within 3 months. But, as on today the Jdr has not complied with the said order. After registration of this execution petition notice has been issued to the Jdr he appeared through his counsel and undertaken to vacate the premises within one month but he has not vacated the premises and not paid the arrears. Court has issued delivery warrant and accordingly, bailiff has open the lock as per the order of this Court and submitted list of inventories on 13.09.2023. Thereafter, 23.01.2024, 27.06.2024, and 05.07.2024 the Jdr counsel has appeared before this Court and undertaken that Jdr will lift the inventories from the premises and inspite of which the Jdr has not complied with the order of this Court. For one or other reason Jdr has filing application and try to obstruct Dhr in taking possession of the property. Ultimately, the Court vide order dated.21.03.2025 directed the bailiff of this Court to conduct auction of the inventories as per law. Accordingly, the bailiff have conducted the auction of the inventories. Bailiff submitted his report, wherein it stated that as per the orders of this court. He has conducted the Public auction of the inventories/movables articles on 19.04.2024 in the schedule premises. Out of 14 movables 8 items have been purchased by D.C.Shivaramegowda and 6 items have been purchased by L.P.Nagaraj through public auction. On that day the auction was concluded in the evening hours and such they could not able the bid amount. Today the auction purchasers are present before the Court and they are ready to paying the bid amount of Rs.33,200/- and Rs.8,000/-. metadata.Order Procedural History: EX 634/2023 Case called out. Learned counsel for DHR present. IA filed by DHR under Sec.39, 40 read with Sec.151 of the CPC. Heard counsel for the DHR and perused the records. The DHR intends to transfer the petition to the jurisdictional court. As per Sec.39 of CPC if such person has no property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the court which pass the decree and has property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other court and if the person against whom the decree is passed resides within the local limits of the jurisdiction such other court, then the court which passes the decree may send it for execution to such other court and transfer the decree to such other court. On perusal of the execution petition it reveals that the JDR No.1 and 2 are residing at Nandanam Exension, Chennai, Tamil Nadu-600035. Hence, by applying the above provision the decree can be transferred to the court as sought in the application. With this observation, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER IA.No. filed by DHR under Sec.39 of CPC is hereby allowed. Office is directed to transfer the decree to the Hon’ble City Civil Court, Chennai, City Court House, No.137, PQ +34, High Court Road, Parrys, George Town, Chennai, Tamil Nadu - 600104. Accordingly instant Execution petition is closed and disposed otherwise. (24.03.2025) XXXIX ACC & SJ, B’Luru

hearings.business_text: Heard the arguments of L/d counsel for the JDR on his objection. Wherein he contended that he had kept ready the cash to make the payment to the DHR herein but in fact he has not approached the JDR by seeking the payment by returning the original documents with him. If that aspect is considered, the JDR made out no grounds as to why the warrant of attaching the movables of the JDR to recover the petition claim. If at all the JDR has kept the cash with him he would have deposited the same in the court and sought the execution of decree for recovering the original documents if any in the custody of the DHR. The reason assigned by the JDR for not complying the compromised decree is not reasonable and acceptable thus the objection of the JDR is hereby rejected as no grounds. PF paid. metadata.Order Procedural History: 1 Ex. No.686/2023 Orders on memo of calculation filed on 12.07.2024 As per the said memo of calculation, the decree holder claims the balance amount of Rs. 14,100/- as on 23.04.2024. The JDr No.2 filed detailed objections. On that basis the point for consideration is as under: “Whether the JDRs are liable to make payment of amount as claimed in the memo of calculation ?” Heard the arguments. Perused the materials on record, on that basis, my finding is in the affirmative, for the following: Point: This Execution Petition is filed to enforce the award passed in L.A.C. No.134/2016. As per the 2 award, the JDRs are liable to pay further interest @ 15% p.a., for subsequent years till deposit of entire compensation amount. The said judgment has been passed on 05.01.2023. Subsequently this Execution Petition is filed. Admittedly the JDRs deposited the amount to the Court on 05.03.2024. As per memo of calculation, the balance amount due from the JDRs to the decree holder as on 03.06.2023 is Rs. 1,09,090/- and the said amount has been deposited to the Court on 05.03.2024. Therefore, the entire amount has not been deposited to the Court till 05.03.2024. Admittedly as per the award, the JDRs are liable to pay 15% interest on the balance amount or enhanced amount. The said award has not been challenged by the JDRs. As such, the JDRs are liable to pay 15% interest on the enhanced compensation amount. When the office memo of calculation is not disputed by the JDRs, it has to be inferred that the JDRs are admitting the office memo of calculation. As per the office memo of calculation the
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: 3 balance amount of Rs. 1,09,090/- has been deposited to the Court as on 05.03.2024. Therefore, the JDRs are liable to pay interest @ 15% on Rs. 1,09,090/- from 03.06.2023 till payment of the said amount. Hence, the JDRs are liable to pay the said amount as claimed in the memo of calculation by the decree holder. Hence, objection of the JDr No.2 is that the JDRs are not liable to pay the amount claimed in the memo of calculation, it cannot be accepted. Hence, it has to be over-ruled. Hence, objection filed by the JDr No.2 to the memo of calculation is hereby over- ruled and the JDRs are liable to pay the amount as per the said memo of calculation. Hence, the above point is answered in the affirmative. In the result, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER The objection filed by the JDr No.2 to the memo of calculation is hereby over ruled. JDRs are liable to pay the balance amount as claimed in the memo of calculation. 4 For payment by 10.02.2025. (PADMA PRASAD) II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, & Spl. Judge, Bengaluru. 5

metadata.Order Procedural History: 1 EX.791/2023 Order on I.A.filed Under Sec.151 of C.P.C. by the Judgment-debtor on 1.8.2023 The counsel for Judgment Debtor has filed this application under Section 151 of C.P.C. to recall the delivery warrant Dt.16.12.2023 issued by this Court. 2. In the affidavit annexed to the application, the Judgment-debtor has sworn to the facts that the Decree-holders have filed this Execution Petition for recovery of arrears of rent and also for issuance of delivery warrant. Accordingly this Court has issued delivery warrant on 16.12.2023 in respect of schedule property which is in his possession. In fact as per the agreed terms of the compromise petition, he has got time to pay the arrears of rent till 10th November 2023. He is ready to comply with the terms of the Undertaking given by him in the compromise decree within reasonable time, whereas this Court has issued delivery warrant Dt.16.12.2023. He has already transferred a sum of Rs.13,00,000/- to the account of the Decree-holders by way of RTGS, out of Rs.20 lakhs payable under the compromise decree 2 Ex.No .791/ 2023 towards arrears of rent. He has also transferred another sum of Rs.2 lakhs to the account of the Decree-holders. Hence Rs.5 lakhs is the only due amount to be paid by him to the Decree-holders as per the decree. He had paid Rs.5 lakhs as advance at the time of inception of tenancy, which is still in the hands of the Decree-holders and hence the question of he leaving the premises without paying the arrears, does not arise. If the Decree-holders would get the delivery warrant executed, he will be put to irreparable loss and injury. Hence it is appropriate to recall the delivery warrant issued by this Court. 3. The learned counsel for the Decree- holder has orally objected the said application and his submission was taken on record. 4. Heard both sides on the said application. 5. As per the contention of the learned counsel for the Judgment-debtor, as per the terms and conditions of the compromise decree, the Judgment-debtor had to pay totally a sum of Rs.20 lakhs towards arrears of rent and the same is to be paid on or before
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: 3 Ex.No .791/ 2023 10.8.2023, accordingly he has already paid a total sum of Rs.15,00,000/- through RTGS to the bank account of the Decree-holders and only Rs.5 lakhs is due towards arrears of rent as per the decree. He also stated that the Judgment-debtor had paid a sum of Rs.5 lakhs as advance at the time of inception of tenancy which is still in the hands of the Decree-holders, hence he is not in arrears of rent. 6. It is to be noted that it is admitted by the Judgment-debtor himself that as per the terms and conditions of the decree, he had to pay the arrears of rent due by him to the Decree-holders on or before 10.8.2023. On perusal of the compromise petition available on record, it reveals that both Decree-holders and Judgment-debtor have filed compromise petition in . 7. As per Condition No.3 of the said compromise petition, the Plaintiffs/Decree- holders have agreed that the Defendant/Judgment-debtor shall pay Rs.20 lakhs towards arrears of rent from December 2019 till January 2023 in six monthly 4 Ex.No .791/ 2023 installments with single default clause commencing from 10th of each calender month. As per condition No.4 of said compromise petition, the Decree-holders/ Plaintiffs have granted 1½ years time from the date of compromise to the Defendant/ Judgment-debtor to vacate and handover vacant possession of the suit schedule premises. Therefore as per the above said conditions of the compromise petition, the Judgment-debtor shall pay the entire arrears of rent of Rs.20 lakhs by the end of January 2023 in six monthly installments and he ought to have vacate and handover the vacant possession of the suit schedule premises within 1½ years from the date of filing of compromise petition. 8. It is also stated at para 6 of the compromise petition that the Plaintiffs/Decree-holders have agreed to refund the security deposit of Rs.5 lakhs to the Defendant/ Judgment-debtor at the time of taking over the vacant possession of the schedule property. As per the version of Judgment-debtor as stated in the application, 5 Ex.No .791/ 2023 he had paid Rs.5 lakhs towards advance amount and took possession of the schedule premises as tenant. But as per the terms of the said compromise petition he is entitled for refund of said security deposit of Rs.5 lakhs at the time of vacating the premises and handing over vacant possession. Hence it is clear that the Judgment-debtor ought to have paid the arrears of rent as per the terms and conditions of the compromise petition entered into between both the parties, on or before 10.8.2023. By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also for the aforesaid reasons, I am of the opinion that the present application filed by the Judgment- debtor for recalling the delivery warrant issued by this Court is not tenable and hence liable to be dismissed. Hence the application filed by the Judgment-debtor under Section 151 of C.P.C. to recall the delivery warrant Dt.16.12.2023 issued by this Court is hereby rejected. 9. judicial_order.procedural_history: 1 EX.791/2023 Order on I.A.filed Under Sec.151 of C.P.C. by the Judgment-debtor on 1.8.2023 The counsel for Judgment Debtor has filed this application under Section 151 of C.P.C. to recall the delivery warrant Dt.16.12.2023 issued by this Court. 2. In the affidavit annexed to the application, the Judgment-debtor has sworn to the facts that the Decree-holders have filed this Execution Petition for recovery of arrears of rent and also for issuance of delivery warrant. Accordingly this Court has issued delivery warrant on 16.12.2023 in respect of schedule property which is in his possession. In fact as per the agreed terms of the compromise petition, he has got time to pay the arrears of rent till 10th November 2023. He is ready to comply with the terms of the Undertaking given by him in the compromise decree within reasonable time, whereas this Court has issued delivery warrant Dt.16.12.2023. He has already transferred a sum of Rs.13,00,000/- to the account of the Decree-holders by way of RTGS, out of Rs.20 lakhs payable under the compromise decree 2 Ex.No .791/ 2023 towards arrears of rent. He has also transferred another sum of Rs.2 lakhs to the account of the Decree-holders. Hence Rs.5 lakhs is the only due amount to be paid by him to the Decree-holders as per the decree. He had paid Rs.5 lakhs as advance at the time of inception of tenancy, which is still in the hands of the Decree-holders and hence the question of he leaving the premises without paying the arrears, does not arise. If the Decree-holders would get the delivery warrant executed, he will be put to irreparable loss and injury. Hence it is appropriate to recall the delivery warrant issued by this Court. 3. The learned counsel for the Decree- holder has orally objected the said application and his submission was taken on record. 4. Heard both sides on the said application. 5. As per the contention of the learned counsel for the Judgment-debtor, as per the terms and conditions of the compromise decree, the Judgment-debtor had to pay totally a sum of Rs.20 lakhs towards arrears of rent and the same is to be paid on or before
judicial_order.judicial_findings: 3 Ex.No .791/ 2023 10.8.2023, accordingly he has already paid a total sum of Rs.15,00,000/- through RTGS to the bank account of the Decree-holders and only Rs.5 lakhs is due towards arrears of rent as per the decree. He also stated that the Judgment-debtor had paid a sum of Rs.5 lakhs as advance at the time of inception of tenancy which is still in the hands of the Decree-holders, hence he is not in arrears of rent. 6. It is to be noted that it is admitted by the Judgment-debtor himself that as per the terms and conditions of the decree, he had to pay the arrears of rent due by him to the Decree-holders on or before 10.8.2023. On perusal of the compromise petition available on record, it reveals that both Decree-holders and Judgment-debtor have filed compromise petition in . 7. As per Condition No.3 of the said compromise petition, the Plaintiffs/Decree- holders have agreed that the Defendant/Judgment-debtor shall pay Rs.20 lakhs towards arrears of rent from December 2019 till January 2023 in six monthly 4 Ex.No .791/ 2023 installments with single default clause commencing from 10th of each calender month. As per condition No.4 of said compromise petition, the Decree-holders/ Plaintiffs have granted 1½ years time from the date of compromise to the Defendant/ Judgment-debtor to vacate and handover vacant possession of the suit schedule premises. Therefore as per the above said conditions of the compromise petition, the Judgment-debtor shall pay the entire arrears of rent of Rs.20 lakhs by the end of January 2023 in six monthly installments and he ought to have vacate and handover the vacant possession of the suit schedule premises within 1½ years from the date of filing of compromise petition. 8. It is also stated at para 6 of the compromise petition that the Plaintiffs/Decree-holders have agreed to refund the security deposit of Rs.5 lakhs to the Defendant/ Judgment-debtor at the time of taking over the vacant possession of the schedule property. As per the version of Judgment-debtor as stated in the application, 5 Ex.No .791/ 2023 he had paid Rs.5 lakhs towards advance amount and took possession of the schedule premises as tenant. But as per the terms of the said compromise petition he is entitled for refund of said security deposit of Rs.5 lakhs at the time of vacating the premises and handing over vacant possession. Hence it is clear that the Judgment-debtor ought to have paid the arrears of rent as per the terms and conditions of the compromise petition entered into between both the parties, on or before 10.8.2023. By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also for the aforesaid reasons, I am of the opinion that the present application filed by the Judgment- debtor for recalling the delivery warrant issued by this Court is not tenable and hence liable to be dismissed. Hence the application filed by the Judgment-debtor under Section 151 of C.P.C. to recall the delivery warrant Dt.16.12.2023 issued by this Court is hereby rejected. 9. hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: BOTH counsel present. On perusal of the order of Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in Writ Petition No.22104/23 dated 04-03-2024 it reflects that being aggrieved by the order dated 09-03-2023 in Chit AppealNo.JRB/Chits/Appeal/20/ 2022-23, JDR has approached the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka. In the writ petition on 04-03-2024 Hon’ble High Court has passed the order, which reads thus:- “The petitioner calls in question rejection of an appeal on 20-03-2023 under the Chit Fund Act. The plea projected by the petitioner is on the same set of facts, the proceedings had been initiated under Sec.138 of the NI Act, 1881 and the petitioner has been convicted and therefore, it would amount to dual proceedings initiated on the same set of facts. The matter require consideration, there shall be interim order of stay as prayed for, till the next date of hearing. In the note it is also noted that as an interim relief, it is prayed that the petitioner herein being aggrieved by the order dated 20-03-2023 passed by the 1st respondent in Chit AppealNo.JRB/Chits/Appeal/20/ 2022-23. Therefore, this is a fit and proper case for staying further proceedings in order dated 20-03-2024 passed by the 1st respondent.” By virtue of this order on perusal of the present execution petition, decree holder has filed execution petition for recovery of Rs.48,66,116/- as a result of order in dispute No.DRB/4th zone / CFS / 43/ 2016-17. But that order was challenged before the Appellate authority in Chit AppealNo.JRB/Chits/Appeal/20/ 2022-23. That appeal was dismissed on 20-03-2023, but the above said order is stayed by the Hon’ble High Court in W.P.No.22104/23 on 04-03-2024. In view of the pendency of the writ petition, execution petition does not survive for consideration at this stage. The present execution petition is closed with liberty to both the parties to file fresh execution petition after the disposal of the writ petition.

hearings.business_text: ಡಿ.ಹೆಚ್‍.ಆರ್ ಪರ ವಕೀಲರು ಮಾನ್ಯ ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯಕ್ಕೆ ಮಧ್ಯಂತರ ಅರ್ಜಿ 2 ದಿವಾಣಿ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯಾ ಸಂಹಿತೆ ಕಲಂ 151ರಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿ, ಜೆ.ಡಿ.ಆರ್ ಇವರು ದಾವಾ ಸ್ವತ್ತಿಗೆ ಬೀಗ ಹಾಕಿದ್ದು, ಬೀಗ ಹೊಡೆದು ಸ್ವಾಧೀನವನ್ನು ಪೋಲಿಸರ ಸಹಾಯದಿಂದ ಜೆ.ಡಿ.ಆರ್ ಇವರಿಂದ ಡಿ.ಹೆಚ್‍.ಆರ್ ಇವರಿಗೆ ಕೊಡಿಸಬೇಕೆಂದು ವಿನಂತಿಸಿಕೊಂಡಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಅರ್ಜಿ ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಪತ್ರ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಲಾಗಿ, ದಾವಾ ಆಸ್ತಿಯ ಸ್ವಾಧೀನವನ್ನು ಕೊಡಿಸಲು ಡೆಲಿವರಿ ವಾರೆಂಟನ್ನು ಹೊರಡಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ಆ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯದ ಬೇಲೀಫರು ದಿನಾಂಕಃ 19-04-2023ರಂದು ದಾವಾ ಆಸ್ತಿಯ ಬಳಿಗೆ ಹೋದಾಗ, ಜೆ.ಡಿ.ಆರ್ ಇವರು ಸ್ವಾಧೀನ ಕ್ರಮ ಜರುಗಿಸಲು ಹೋದಾಗ ಜೆ.ಡಿ.ಆರ್‍ ರವರು ದಾವಾ ಸ್ವತ್ತಿಗೆ ಬೀಗ ಹಾಕಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಸ್ವಾಧೀನವನ್ನು ಡಿ.ಹೆಚ್‍.ಆರ್ ಇವರಿಗೆ ಕೊಡಿಸಲು ಪೋಲೀಸರ ಸಹಾಯ ನೀಡಬೇಕೆಂದು, ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಪತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ತಿಳಿಸಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಸದರಿ ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಪತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿರತಕ್ಕಂತಹ ವಿಷಯಕ್ಕನುಗುಣವಾಗಿ, ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯದ ಬೇಲೀಫರು ವರದಿ ಹಾಗೂ ಸ್ಥಳ ಮಹಜರನ್ನೂ ಸಹಿತ ಕೊಟ್ಟಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಸದರಿ ದಾಖಲೆಗಳ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಅರ್ಜಿ ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಪತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿರತಕ್ಕಂತಹ ವಿಷಯಗಳು ಸಕಾರಣಗಳಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿರುವುದರಿಂದ, ಈ ಕೆಳಗಿನಂತೆಃ ಆದೇಶ ಡಿ.ಹೆಚ್‍.ಆರ್ ಪರ ವಕೀಲರು ಮಾನ್ಯ ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯಕ್ಕೆ ಮಧ್ಯಂತರ ಅರ್ಜಿ 2 ದಿವಾಣಿ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯಾ ಸಂಹಿತೆ ಕಲಂ 151ರ ಅರ್ಜಿಯನ್ನು ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ದಾವಾ ಆಸ್ತಿಯ ಸ್ವಾಧೀನಮ್ನ ಜೆ.ಡಿ.ಆರ್ ಇವರ ಕಡೆಯಿಂದ ಡಿ.ಹೆಚ್‍.ಆರ್ ಇವರಿಗೆ ಕೊಡಿಸಲು ಪುನಃ ಡೆಲಿವರಿ ವಾರೆಂಟ್‍ ಕಳುಹಿಸಲು ಆದೇಶಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ಒಂದು ವೇಳೆ ಜೆ.ಡಿ.ಆರ್ ಇವರು ದಾವಾ ಆಸ್ತಿ ಮನೆಗೆ ಬೀಗ ಹಾಕಿದ್ದಲ್ಲಿ, ಬೀಗವನ್ನು ಹೊಡೆದು ದಾವಾ ಆಸ್ತಿಯ ಸ್ವಾಧೀನವನ್ನು ಡಿ.ಹೆಚ್‍.ಆರ್ ಇವರಿಗೆ ಕೊಡಿಸಲು ಆದೇಶಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ದಾವಾ ಆಸ್ತಿಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಪಟ್ಟಂತಹ ಸ್ಥಳೀಯ ಪೋಲೀಸ್‍ ಠಾಣಾ ಅಧಿಕಾರಿಯವರು ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯದ ಬೇಲೀಫರು ಜೆ.ಡಿ.ಆರ್ ಇವರಿಂದ ಡಿ.ಹೆಚ್‍.ಆರ್ ಗೆ ಸ್ವಾಧೀನ ಕೊಡಿಸುವ ಸಂಬಂಧಪಟ್ಟಂತೆ ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯದ ಬೇಲೀಫರಿಗೆ ರಕ್ಷಣೆ ನೀಡುವಂತೆ ಆದೇಶಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ಪಿ.ಎಫ್‍ ತುಂಬಿದ ನಂತರ ಡೆಲಿವರಿ ವಾರೆಂಟ್ ಕಳುಹಿಸಲು ಆದೇಶಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ಸದರಿ ಮಾಹಿತಿಯನ್ನು ಸಂಬಂಧಪಟ್ಟಂತಹ ಠಾಣಾ ಅಧಿಕಾರಿಯವರಿಗೆ ಕಳುಹಿಸಲು ಆದೇಶಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ಮುಂದಿನ ದಿನಾಂಕಃ 15-06-2023.

metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 14/01/2026] 5 Ex.No.923/2023 9. It is well settled law that the executing court cannot go beyond the decree. In other words, if the decree is not passed directing the judgment debtor to pay the interest and if the judgment debtor has not paid the decreetal amount within the specified time, the executing court cannot fix the interest and direct the payment of interest for the delayed payment. The decree holder should have sought such a relief in the original suit itself. Since such an order is not passed in the suit, the executing court cannot rewrite the decree. Therefore, though the decree holder is justified in expressing his grievance for the delayed payment, it is beyond the scope of the executing court to fix the rate of interest and direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the non- payment of amount immediately after passing of the decree. No.923/2023 Decree Holder: Sri A. Lakshmipathy s/o Late L. Andanappa Aged about 60 years R/at No.7, 4th ‘A’ Cross M.M. Layout, Kavalbyrasandra Bengaluru-560 032. (In person) Vs. Judgment Debtor: Smt.Venkatalakshmi (Dead by Lrs) 1(a) Sri Vishwachari @ Vishweshwarachar H/o Venkatalakshmi Aged about 52 years 1(b) Sri Jagadeesh s/o Venkatalakshmi & Vishwachari Aged about 26 years 1(c) Sri Sharat s/o Venkatalakshmi & Vishwachari Aged about 21 years All are r/at No.7, Ground Floor Maheshwaramma Temple Street J.C.Nagar, Bengaluru-560 006. (By Sri S. Shankarachar, Adv.) 2 Ex.No.923/2023 I.As.No.5 & 6 Applicant: Sri A. Lakshmipathy - Decree Holder v/s Opponents: Smt.Venkatalakshmi (Dead by Lrs) - Judgment Debtor Provision under which the applications are filed - U/S 151 CPC Reliefs sought for - Direction to pay interest for the delayed payment and to issue attachment warrant The date on which the applications are filed - 10.10.2025 Number of the applications - I.As.No.5 & 6 The date on which the objections are filed by different opponents - 24.10.2025 The date on which the orders were passed on the said application - 14.01.2026 ORDERS ON I.As.No.5 & 6 I.A.No.5 is filed by the decree holder under Section 151 CPC to direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest on the decreetal amount and I.A.No.6 is filed by the decree holder under Section 151 CPC for issuance of attachment warrant for the recovery of amount. 2. The decree holder in the application has contended that the judgment debtor has caused unnecessary delay in payment of the decreetal amount after passing of the decree and therefore the judgment debtor is liable to pay interest of Rs.2,53,026/-.
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: 3 Ex.No.923/2023 3. The application is seriously objected by the judgement debtor contending that payment of interest to the decreetal amount is not contemplated in the decree and therefore the decree holder cannot claim the interest. 4. Heard the arguments. 5. The points for determination of this Court are:- 1) Whether in an execution petition, the executing court can direct the judgment debtor to pay interest on the decreetal amount for the delay caused by the judgment debtor in paying the decreetal amount if such interest is not ordered to be paid in the decree? 2) What order? 6. Finding of this Court on the above points are as hereunder:- :- In the negative :- As per final order, for the following:- - : : - 7. POINT No.1:- It is an admitted fact that in the decree passed by this Court while passing an order of ejectment directed the judgment debtor to pay rent of 7,000/- per month from ₹ 22.08.2017 to 22.07.2023 for a period of 72 months till the date of delivery of possession of the petition schedule property. It is also not in dispute that the amount payable is Rs.5,04,000/- and the 4 Ex.No.923/2023 decree holder is also entitled for costs of the suit to the tune of Rs.36,099/-. Further, in the decree, the Court has directed to deduct a sum of 2,50,000/- paid by the judgment debtor to the ₹ decree holder as security deposit. Therefore, it is an admitted fact that the total liability payable by the judgment debtor to the decree holder was Rs.2,90,099/- and the entire amount of 2,90,099/- is ₹ paid by the judgment debtor. But, the amount was not paid immediately after passing of the decree or filing of the execution petition. Initially a sum of 80,000/- was paid and later Rs.1 lakh ₹ was paid on 12.08.2025 and the remaining amount of 1,10,099/- ₹ was paid on 17.09.2025. In this way, the decreetal amount is cleared. 8. The grievance of the decree holder is that the judgement debtor has not paid the amount immediately after passing of the decree and therefore he is liable to pay interest for the delayed payment. It is true that when the Court has passed the decree, the judgment debtor should have paid the entire amount immediately after passing of the decree. The delay caused in payment of the decreetal amount has resulted loss to the judgment debtor. But, the question for consideration is when the decree do not contemplate payment of interest for the delayed payment, whether the executing court can direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the delayed payment. 5 Ex.No.923/2023 9. It is well settled law that the executing court cannot go beyond the decree. In other words, if the decree is not passed directing the judgment debtor to pay the interest and if the judgment debtor has not paid the decreetal amount within the specified time, the executing court cannot fix the interest and direct the payment of interest for the delayed payment. The decree holder should have sought such a relief in the original suit itself. Since such an order is not passed in the suit, the executing court cannot rewrite the decree. Therefore, though the decree holder is justified in expressing his grievance for the delayed payment, it is beyond the scope of the executing court to fix the rate of interest and direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the non- payment of amount immediately after passing of the decree. Further, in the decree, the Court has not even fixed the time limit for the payment of the decreetal amount. Under these circumstances, this Court, being an executing court is unable to compensate the decree holder by directing the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the delayed payment. In view of this, the court cannot direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest as claimed by the decree holder. Accordingly, point No.1 is answered in the negative. 10. :- In view of the answer given to point No.1 in the negative, this court cannot direct the judgment debtor to pay
metadata.Order Annexed Proceedings: 6 Ex.No.923/2023 the interest for the delayed payment. The amount as decreed in the original suit is paid by the judgment debtor therefore, the execution is required to be closed as fully satisfied. However, it is made clear that decree holder is at liberty to pursue his remedy for mesne profits as directed in the decree without being influenced by the observations made in the present order. Accordingly, the following order is passed:- O R D E R I.A.No.5 & 6 filed by the decree holder to direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the delayed payment are rejected. The execution petition is closed as fully satisfied. However, it is made clear that the decree holder is at liberty to seek mesne profits as directed in the decree without being affected by the disposal of this execution petition. judicial_order.operative_ruling: [Order Dated: 14/01/2026] 5 Ex.No.923/2023 9. It is well settled law that the executing court cannot go beyond the decree. In other words, if the decree is not passed directing the judgment debtor to pay the interest and if the judgment debtor has not paid the decreetal amount within the specified time, the executing court cannot fix the interest and direct the payment of interest for the delayed payment. The decree holder should have sought such a relief in the original suit itself. Since such an order is not passed in the suit, the executing court cannot rewrite the decree. Therefore, though the decree holder is justified in expressing his grievance for the delayed payment, it is beyond the scope of the executing court to fix the rate of interest and direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the non- payment of amount immediately after passing of the decree. Further, in the decree, the Court has not even fixed the time limit for the payment of the decreetal amount. Under these circumstances, this Court, being an executing court is unable to compensate the decree holder by directing the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the delayed payment. In view of this, the court cannot direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest as claimed by the decree holder. Accordingly, point No.1 is answered in the negative. 10. :- In view of the answer given to point No.1 in the negative, this court cannot direct the judgment debtor to pay
