No.923/2023 Decree Holder: Sri A. Lakshmipathy s/o Late L. Andanappa Aged about 60 years R/at No.7, 4th ‘A’ Cross M.M. Layout, Kavalbyrasandra Bengaluru-560 032. (In person) Vs. Judgment Debtor: Smt.Venkatalakshmi (Dead by Lrs) 1(a) Sri Vishwachari @ Vishweshwarachar H/o Venkatalakshmi Aged about 52 years 1(b) Sri Jagadeesh s/o Venkatalakshmi & Vishwachari Aged about 26 years 1(c) Sri Sharat s/o Venkatalakshmi & Vishwachari Aged about 21 years All are r/at No.7, Ground Floor Maheshwaramma Temple Street J.C.Nagar, Bengaluru-560 006. (By Sri S. Shankarachar, Adv.) 2 Ex.No.923/2023 I.As.No.5 & 6 Applicant: Sri A. Lakshmipathy - Decree Holder v/s Opponents: Smt.Venkatalakshmi (Dead by Lrs) - Judgment Debtor Provision under which the applications are filed - U/S 151 CPC Reliefs sought for - Direction to pay interest for the delayed payment and to issue attachment warrant The date on which the applications are filed - 10.10.2025 Number of the applications - I.As.No.5 & 6 The date on which the objections are filed by different opponents - 24.10.2025 The date on which the orders were passed on the said application - 14.01.2026 ORDERS ON I.As.No.5 & 6 I.A.No.5 is filed by the decree holder under Section 151 CPC to direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest on the decreetal amount and I.A.No.6 is filed by the decree holder under Section 151 CPC for issuance of attachment warrant for the recovery of amount. 2. The decree holder in the application has contended that the judgment debtor has caused unnecessary delay in payment of the decreetal amount after passing of the decree and therefore the judgment debtor is liable to pay interest of Rs.2,53,026/-.
judicial_order.judicial_findings: 3 Ex.No.923/2023 3. The application is seriously objected by the judgement debtor contending that payment of interest to the decreetal amount is not contemplated in the decree and therefore the decree holder cannot claim the interest. 4. Heard the arguments. 5. The points for determination of this Court are:- 1) Whether in an execution petition, the executing court can direct the judgment debtor to pay interest on the decreetal amount for the delay caused by the judgment debtor in paying the decreetal amount if such interest is not ordered to be paid in the decree? 2) What order? 6. Finding of this Court on the above points are as hereunder:- :- In the negative :- As per final order, for the following:- - : : - 7. POINT No.1:- It is an admitted fact that in the decree passed by this Court while passing an order of ejectment directed the judgment debtor to pay rent of 7,000/- per month from ₹ 22.08.2017 to 22.07.2023 for a period of 72 months till the date of delivery of possession of the petition schedule property. It is also not in dispute that the amount payable is Rs.5,04,000/- and the 4 Ex.No.923/2023 decree holder is also entitled for costs of the suit to the tune of Rs.36,099/-. Further, in the decree, the Court has directed to deduct a sum of 2,50,000/- paid by the judgment debtor to the ₹ decree holder as security deposit. Therefore, it is an admitted fact that the total liability payable by the judgment debtor to the decree holder was Rs.2,90,099/- and the entire amount of 2,90,099/- is ₹ paid by the judgment debtor. But, the amount was not paid immediately after passing of the decree or filing of the execution petition. Initially a sum of 80,000/- was paid and later Rs.1 lakh ₹ was paid on 12.08.2025 and the remaining amount of 1,10,099/- ₹ was paid on 17.09.2025. In this way, the decreetal amount is cleared. 8. The grievance of the decree holder is that the judgement debtor has not paid the amount immediately after passing of the decree and therefore he is liable to pay interest for the delayed payment. It is true that when the Court has passed the decree, the judgment debtor should have paid the entire amount immediately after passing of the decree. The delay caused in payment of the decreetal amount has resulted loss to the judgment debtor. But, the question for consideration is when the decree do not contemplate payment of interest for the delayed payment, whether the executing court can direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the delayed payment. 5 Ex.No.923/2023 9. It is well settled law that the executing court cannot go beyond the decree. In other words, if the decree is not passed directing the judgment debtor to pay the interest and if the judgment debtor has not paid the decreetal amount within the specified time, the executing court cannot fix the interest and direct the payment of interest for the delayed payment. The decree holder should have sought such a relief in the original suit itself. Since such an order is not passed in the suit, the executing court cannot rewrite the decree. Therefore, though the decree holder is justified in expressing his grievance for the delayed payment, it is beyond the scope of the executing court to fix the rate of interest and direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the non- payment of amount immediately after passing of the decree. Further, in the decree, the Court has not even fixed the time limit for the payment of the decreetal amount. Under these circumstances, this Court, being an executing court is unable to compensate the decree holder by directing the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the delayed payment. In view of this, the court cannot direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest as claimed by the decree holder. Accordingly, point No.1 is answered in the negative. 10. :- In view of the answer given to point No.1 in the negative, this court cannot direct the judgment debtor to pay
judicial_order.annexed_proceedings: 6 Ex.No.923/2023 the interest for the delayed payment. The amount as decreed in the original suit is paid by the judgment debtor therefore, the execution is required to be closed as fully satisfied. However, it is made clear that decree holder is at liberty to pursue his remedy for mesne profits as directed in the decree without being influenced by the observations made in the present order. Accordingly, the following order is passed:- O R D E R I.A.No.5 & 6 filed by the decree holder to direct the judgment debtor to pay the interest for the delayed payment are rejected. The execution petition is closed as fully satisfied. However, it is made clear that the decree holder is at liberty to seek mesne profits as directed in the decree without being affected by the disposal of this execution petition. metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 14/09/2023] :: Acting U/Sec. 39 (1) of CPC the decree is hereby transfered to Hon’ble District & Sessions Court, Ramanagara, for execution of decree passed in O.S.5576/2019. Office to send the records to above court as per law. Issue DTR. Accordingly memo is disposed off. XIV ACC & SJ, Bengaluru.
metadata.Order Procedural History: CCH-28 Ex.No.961/2023 14.09.2023 For order Learned counsel for decree holder has filed a memo seeking an order to transfer the decree to District & Sessions Judge, at Ramanagara. 2. Learned counsel for Decree Holder submitted that, judgment debtor JDR.No.1 & 2 are residing within the jurisdiction of above Court and therefore he prays to transfer the decree. 3. Heard arguments of learned counsel for decree holder and perused the materials placed on record. At the time of argument, learned counsel for decree holder requested for transfer of decree. CCH-28 Ex.No.961/2023 4. Sec.39 of CPC enables the court which passed the decree send the decree to another court of competent jurisdiction for execution. The provision enables the court to send the decree for execution to another Court of competent jurisdiction. The cause title of judgment passed in O.S.5576/2019 and Execution petition on hand clearly reveals that, defendant/Jdr No.1 & 2 are residing at Chikkamukkadlu, Bannimukkadlu Post, Kodahalli Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District. The Jdr’s have not deposited or paid the decreetal amount to Dhr. Therefore, learned counsel for Dhr., requested for transfer of decree to Hon’ble District & Sessions Court, Ramanagara. Hence, following :: ORDER :: Acting U/Sec. 39 (1) of CPC the decree is hereby transfered to Hon’ble District & Sessions Court, Ramanagara, for execution of decree passed in O.S.5576/2019. Office to send the records to above court as per law. Issue DTR. Accordingly memo is disposed off. XIV ACC & SJ, Bengaluru.
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: CCH-28 Ex.No.961/2023 4. Sec.39 of CPC enables the court which passed the decree send the decree to another court of competent jurisdiction for execution. The provision enables the court to send the decree for execution to another Court of competent jurisdiction. metadata.Order Procedural History: Ex.No. 1049/2023 Orders on application filed by the DHR under order 21 rule 35 r/w sec. 151 OF CPC. The Decree holder has filed present application praying to issue delivery warrant with break open lock with police help. The decree holder has filed the present petitioner praying for execution of decree in OS.No. 4927/2021 and prayed for delivery of possession of the suit property by issuing delivery warrant. It is to be noted here that vide order dated 21­06­2023, this court after considering the case of the decree holder had issued delivery warrant. The said delivery warrant was not executed and it was returned with shara by the bailiff stating that, the suit property was locked. As such, the decree holder has filed the present application praying to break open the lock for execution of delivery warrant. Order 21 Rule 35(3) gives power to this court to order for break opening any door or to do any act necessary for putting the decree holder in possession of property. Since the suit schedule property is locked, breaking open the lock is very much necessary for execution of the decree and to deliver the possession of the suit property to the decree holder. If the order to break open lock with police help is not granted, the decree holder will be put to hardship and very purpose of filing the petition will be defeated. If the order for breaking open of lock is granted by the bailiff only, there is chances that JDR may make galata. As such, I am of the opinion that necessary police help should be granted to the bailiff to execute the warrant. Hence, I am of the opinion that the application can be allowed. Accordingly I proceed to pass the following; ORDER Application filed by the DHR under Order 21 Rule 35 R/w Sec. 151 of CPC., is hereby allowed. Issue delivery warrant with break open lock, with police help if PF paid. Call on 11­10­2023. LII A.C.C.& S.J., Bengaluru.

As such, I am of the opinion that necessary police help should be granted to the bailiff to execute the warrant. Hence, I am of the opinion that the application can be allowed. Accordingly I proceed to pass the following; ORDER Application filed by the DHR under Order 21 Rule 35 R/w Sec. 151 of CPC., is hereby allowed. Issue delivery warrant with break open lock, with police help if PF paid. Call on 11­10­2023. LII A.C.C.& S.J., Bengaluru.

metadata.Order Procedural History: IN THE COURT OF THE XI ADDL. CITY CIVIL & SESSIONS JUDGE, BENGALURU CITY (CCH-8) PRESENT SRI. B.DASARATHA, B.A., LL.B., XI Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City. DATED THIS THE 6 th DAY OF APRIL, 2026 Execution Case No.1055/2023 Decree-holder: Sri. L.A.Krishnappa, S/o. Late Anjanappa, Aged about 73 years, R/at Raghavendra Nilaya, No.131, Laggere Main Road, Bengaluru – 560 058. (By Adv. Sri. A.Venkata Reddy) Vs. Judgment-debtor: Sri. A.Narasimha Murthy, S/o. Late Anantharamaiah, Aged about 79 years, Residing at No.7, Behind Lakshminarayana Temple, Settyhalli Village, Jalahalli Post, Bengaluru – 560 015. (By Adv. Indrani L) 2 Ex. No.1055/2023 Provision under which the application is filed : Section 151 of CPC Relief sought for : Seeking direction to obtain the consent signature of the judgment-debtor for execution and registration of the sale deed Date on which the application is filed : 04.02.2026 Number of the application : I.A. No.3 Date on which the objections are filed by different opponents : Counsel for judgment-debtor has no objection to allow I.A. No.3. Date on which orders were passed on the said application : 06.04.2026 Stage of filing of IA : Execution of Sale Deed ORDERS ON I.A. No.3 This application is filed by the decree-holder under Section 151 of CPC, seeking direction to permit/secure the signature of the judgment-debtor - Sri.A.Narasimha Murthy, as a consenting witness to the sale deed to be executed in pursuance of the decree passed in the present execution proceedings.
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: 3 Ex. No.1055/2023 2. The Counsel for judgment-debtor has no objection to allow I.A. No.3. 3. Heard the arguments. 4. Now, the points that would arise for my consideration are :- 1. Whether the decree-holder has made out sufficient grounds to allow I.A. No.3 filed under Section 151 of CPC seeking direction to obtain the consent signature of the judgment-debtor for execution and registration of the sale deed? 2. What order? 5. My findings on the above points are as under:- : In the affirmative. : As per final order below for the following; 6. :- The records disclose that the present Execution Petition is filed for enforcement of the decree directing execution of sale deed in respect of land, measuring 1 acre in Sy. 4 Ex. No.1055/2023 No.77 of Shettyhalli Village, Yeshwanthpur Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, out of total extent of 2 acres. It is not in dispute that, the remaining 1 acre is retained by the judgment-debtor. 7. The decree-holder has placed on record the communication issued by the Sub-Registrar, Peenya, which clearly indicates that, due to technical constraints in the Kaveri-2 portal, the registration of sale deed for 1 acre alone is not being permitted since the 11-E sketch reflects the entire extent of 2 acres jointly. It is further evident from the endorsement that, unless the land is distinctly reflected or unless the consent/signature of the co-holder (judgment-debtor) is secured, the system does not permit registration of the sale deed. Thus, the difficulty projected by the decree-holder is not legal in nature, but procedural/technical arising out of the digitized registration process. The decree already entitles the decree-holder to obtain the registered sale deed in respect of 1 acre. However, due to the technical impediment in the registration process, execution of the decree has become impracticable unless appropriate directions are issued by this court. 8. It is pertinent to note that, the Learned Counsel for 5 Ex. No.1055/2023 judgment-debtor has filed vakalath and has submitted no objection to the allowing of this application. The absence of objection from the judgment-debtor further fortifies the case of decree-holder. 9. This court, being an Executing Court, is empowered not only to enforce the decree, but also to remove all ancillary and procedural obstacles that hinder its effective implementation. The inherent powers under Section 151 of CPC can be invoked to ensure that the decree does not become inexecutable on account of technical or administrative hurdles. 10. If the relief sought is not granted, the decree-holder, despite having a valid decree in his favour, would be deprived of the fruits of the decree, which would result in grave injustice. On the other hand, no prejudice will be caused to the judgment- debtor, especially when he has not opposed the application. 11. Therefore, this court is of the considered opinion that, it is just and necessary to permit and direct the judgment-debtor to affix his signature as a consenting witness to facilitate registration
metadata.Order Annexed Proceedings: 6 Ex. No.1055/2023 of the sale deed in favour of the decree-holder. Accordingly, is answered in the affirmative. 12. :- In view of the above discussions, this court proceed to pass the following:- ORDER I.A. No.3 filed by the decree-holder under Section 151 of CPC is hereby allowed. The judgment-debtor - Sri.A.Narasimha Murthy, is hereby directed to affix his signature as a consenting witness to the sale deed to be executed in favour of the decree-holder in respect of 1 acre of land in Sy. No.77 of Shettyhalli Village. No order as to costs. (Dictated to the Stenographer Grade-I directly on computer, typed by her, corrected and then pronounced by me, in the open court, this the 6th day of April, 2026) (B.DASARATHA) XI ADDL. CITY CIVIL & SESSIONS JUDGE BENGALURU CITY.

judicial_order.operative_ruling: [Order Dated: 06/04/2026] 5 Ex. No.1055/2023 judgment-debtor has filed vakalath and has submitted no objection to the allowing of this application. The absence of objection from the judgment-debtor further fortifies the case of decree-holder. 9. This court, being an Executing Court, is empowered not only to enforce the decree, but also to remove all ancillary and procedural obstacles that hinder its effective implementation. The inherent powers under Section 151 of CPC can be invoked to ensure that the decree does not become inexecutable on account of technical or administrative hurdles. 10. If the relief sought is not granted, the decree-holder, despite having a valid decree in his favour, would be deprived of the fruits of the decree, which would result in grave injustice. On the other hand, no prejudice will be caused to the judgment- debtor, especially when he has not opposed the application. 11. Therefore, this court is of the considered opinion that, it is just and necessary to permit and direct the judgment-debtor to affix his signature as a consenting witness to facilitate registration
judicial_order.procedural_history: IN THE COURT OF THE XI ADDL. CITY CIVIL & SESSIONS JUDGE, BENGALURU CITY (CCH-8) PRESENT SRI. B.DASARATHA, B.A., LL.B., XI Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City. DATED THIS THE 6 th DAY OF APRIL, 2026 Execution Case No.1055/2023 Decree-holder: Sri. L.A.Krishnappa, S/o. Late Anjanappa, Aged about 73 years, R/at Raghavendra Nilaya, No.131, Laggere Main Road, Bengaluru – 560 058. (By Adv. Sri. A.Venkata Reddy) Vs. Judgment-debtor: Sri. A.Narasimha Murthy, S/o. Late Anantharamaiah, Aged about 79 years, Residing at No.7, Behind Lakshminarayana Temple, Settyhalli Village, Jalahalli Post, Bengaluru – 560 015. (By Adv. Indrani L) 2 Ex. No.1055/2023 Provision under which the application is filed : Section 151 of CPC Relief sought for : Seeking direction to obtain the consent signature of the judgment-debtor for execution and registration of the sale deed Date on which the application is filed : 04.02.2026 Number of the application : I.A. No.3 Date on which the objections are filed by different opponents : Counsel for judgment-debtor has no objection to allow I.A. No.3. Date on which orders were passed on the said application : 06.04.2026 Stage of filing of IA : Execution of Sale Deed ORDERS ON I.A. No.3 This application is filed by the decree-holder under Section 151 of CPC, seeking direction to permit/secure the signature of the judgment-debtor - Sri.A.Narasimha Murthy, as a consenting witness to the sale deed to be executed in pursuance of the decree passed in the present execution proceedings.
judicial_order.judicial_findings: 3 Ex. No.1055/2023 2. The Counsel for judgment-debtor has no objection to allow I.A. No.3. 3. Heard the arguments. 4. Now, the points that would arise for my consideration are :- 1. Whether the decree-holder has made out sufficient grounds to allow I.A. No.3 filed under Section 151 of CPC seeking direction to obtain the consent signature of the judgment-debtor for execution and registration of the sale deed? 2. What order? 5. My findings on the above points are as under:- : In the affirmative. : As per final order below for the following; 6. :- The records disclose that the present Execution Petition is filed for enforcement of the decree directing execution of sale deed in respect of land, measuring 1 acre in Sy. 4 Ex. No.1055/2023 No.77 of Shettyhalli Village, Yeshwanthpur Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, out of total extent of 2 acres. It is not in dispute that, the remaining 1 acre is retained by the judgment-debtor. 7. The decree-holder has placed on record the communication issued by the Sub-Registrar, Peenya, which clearly indicates that, due to technical constraints in the Kaveri-2 portal, the registration of sale deed for 1 acre alone is not being permitted since the 11-E sketch reflects the entire extent of 2 acres jointly. It is further evident from the endorsement that, unless the land is distinctly reflected or unless the consent/signature of the co-holder (judgment-debtor) is secured, the system does not permit registration of the sale deed. Thus, the difficulty projected by the decree-holder is not legal in nature, but procedural/technical arising out of the digitized registration process. The decree already entitles the decree-holder to obtain the registered sale deed in respect of 1 acre. However, due to the technical impediment in the registration process, execution of the decree has become impracticable unless appropriate directions are issued by this court. 8. It is pertinent to note that, the Learned Counsel for 5 Ex. No.1055/2023 judgment-debtor has filed vakalath and has submitted no objection to the allowing of this application. The absence of objection from the judgment-debtor further fortifies the case of decree-holder. 9. This court, being an Executing Court, is empowered not only to enforce the decree, but also to remove all ancillary and procedural obstacles that hinder its effective implementation. The inherent powers under Section 151 of CPC can be invoked to ensure that the decree does not become inexecutable on account of technical or administrative hurdles. 10. If the relief sought is not granted, the decree-holder, despite having a valid decree in his favour, would be deprived of the fruits of the decree, which would result in grave injustice. On the other hand, no prejudice will be caused to the judgment- debtor, especially when he has not opposed the application. 11. Therefore, this court is of the considered opinion that, it is just and necessary to permit and direct the judgment-debtor to affix his signature as a consenting witness to facilitate registration
judicial_order.annexed_proceedings: 6 Ex. No.1055/2023 of the sale deed in favour of the decree-holder. Accordingly, is answered in the affirmative. 12. :- In view of the above discussions, this court proceed to pass the following:- ORDER I.A. No.3 filed by the decree-holder under Section 151 of CPC is hereby allowed. The judgment-debtor - Sri.A.Narasimha Murthy, is hereby directed to affix his signature as a consenting witness to the sale deed to be executed in favour of the decree-holder in respect of 1 acre of land in Sy. No.77 of Shettyhalli Village. No order as to costs. (Dictated to the Stenographer Grade-I directly on computer, typed by her, corrected and then pronounced by me, in the open court, this the 6th day of April, 2026) (B.DASARATHA) XI ADDL. CITY CIVIL & SESSIONS JUDGE BENGALURU CITY.

metadata.Case Title: GOVINDARAJ K vs RAVI RAJU
metadata.Court Name: PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Court Room & Judge: 25-CCH6 XXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 26/02/2024] Ex. 1064 /2023 wherein it is held that the Executing Court must take the decree as it stands as it is binding and conclusive between the parties to the suit and also referred Judgment in State of Madhya Pradesh V/s Mangilal Sharma in CD 1997 SC 689 (Supreme Court of India), it is held that,: ‘A Declaratory decree, in my opinion, cannot be executed as it only declares the rights of the decree- holder qua the Judgment Debtor and does not in terms, direct the Judgment Debtor to do or to refrain from doing any particular act or thing. Since there is no command issued to the Judgment Debtor to obey, the civil process cannot be issued for the compliance of that mandate or command. The decree- holder is free to seek his legal remedies by way of suit or otherwise on the basis of the declaration given in his favour..”.
metadata.Order Procedural History: Ex. 1064 /2023 26.2.2024 DHR – K.Govindaraju V/s JDR - Ravi Raju ORDERS ON MAINTAINABILITY The petitioner has filed this petition to execute the decree in O.S.No. 4007 of 2007, wherein the suit was filed for permanent injunction and mandatory injunction with respect to the suit schedule property. The court by order dt. 13.07.2010 was pleased to decree the suit with a direction “It is declared that plaintiff has easementary right over B-schedule property. The defendant or his men, servants attorneys, watchmen or any persons claiming any rights, through or under the defendant are hereby restrained from interfering with the right of way of the plaintiff. The defendant is restrained Ex. 1064 /2023 from putting up any construction on the B- schedule property. The defendant is directed by way of decree of mandatory injunction to remove the illegal structure like Sajja and door facing towards common passage. The Regular First Appeal No.1674 of 2010 was filed challenging the said decree which came to be withdrawn on 22.07.2022. Hence this petition is filed seeking execution of decree in O.S.4007 of 2007. 2. The learned counsel for petitioner has submitted the entire records along with the photographs and prayed that the wall is constructed in 5 feet as such in view of decree the same needs to be removed. In the prayer he has sought for issuing necessary warrant to remove illegal structure like Sajja, Door and wall with pillar facing towards passage of D.H.R residence i.e., ‘B’ schedule
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: Ex. 1064 /2023 property. 3. The J.D.R has appeared and filed objections contending that he has not put any structure over ‘B’ schedule property and he has purchased the property with existing building itself. It was constructed in the year 2000 by his vendor. The report of the Court Commissioner measured 40 feet and the width differs which was not 5 feet as claimed by D.H.R. In the decree he was directed to remove Sajja and door facing towards common passage before the warrant was issued. In Execution Petition No. 685 of 2011, the R.F.A No.1674 of 2010 was preferred. To maintain the peace the JDR has already removed Sajja and door facing ‘B’ schedule property. The DHR stopped Execution petition No.685 of 2011. the same came to be dismissed for default on 17.07.2021. There is no Sajja or door window facing ‘B’ schedule property. There is no illegal Ex. 1064 /2023 construction. Hence prays to dismiss the petition. He has produced the photographs. 4. Heard. The learned counsel for JDR has produced citations and DHR has submitted written arguments along with citations. 5. In view of pleadings by JDR that already the decree is complied by removing Sajja and door facing towards common passage. Perusal of the photographs discloses that, already the wall is plastered by removing the windows and there is no Sajja and common passage left free. Admittedly this is the executing court which cannot go behind the decree which is also upheld in the decision submitted by DHR in the W.P.No. 14696 of 2022 dt. 4.8.2023 and Judgment in Civil Appeal 1312-1313 of 2023 dt. 21.02.2023 in the case of Sanwarlal Agarwal and others V/s Ashok Kumar Kothari and others, Ex. 1064 /2023 wherein it is held that the Executing Court must take the decree as it stands as it is binding and conclusive between the parties to the suit and also referred Judgment in State of Madhya Pradesh V/s Mangilal Sharma in CD 1997 SC 689 (Supreme Court of India), it is held that,: ‘A Declaratory decree, in my opinion, cannot be executed as it only declares the rights of the decree- holder qua the Judgment Debtor and does not in terms, direct the Judgment Debtor to do or to refrain from doing any particular act or thing. Since there is no command issued to the Judgment Debtor to obey, the civil process cannot be issued for the compliance of that mandate or command. The decree- holder is free to seek his legal remedies by way of suit or otherwise on the basis of the declaration given in his favour..”.
metadata.Order Annexed Proceedings: Ex. 1064 /2023 property is right of way reserved to the plaintiff. In view of clear grant of direction to removal of Sajja and Wall this executing court cannot direct removal of wall with pillar which is claimed to be existing in the year 2000 itself, as the entire building stands on the very said wall and pillar. As such the application is not maintainable and the same is hereby rejected. XXIV Addl.City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru

Perusal of the photographs discloses that, already the wall is plastered by removing the windows and there is no Sajja and common passage left free. Admittedly this is the executing court which cannot go behind the decree which is also upheld in the decision submitted by DHR in the W.P.No. 14696 of 2022 dt. 4.8.2023 and Judgment in Civil Appeal 1312-1313 of 2023 dt. 21.02.2023 in the case of Sanwarlal Agarwal and others V/s Ashok Kumar Kothari and others, Ex. 1064 /2023 wherein it is held that the Executing Court must take the decree as it stands as it is binding and conclusive between the parties to the suit and also referred Judgment in State of Madhya Pradesh V/s Mangilal Sharma in CD 1997 SC 689 (Supreme Court of India), it is held that,: ‘A Declaratory decree, in my opinion, cannot be executed as it only declares the rights of the decree- holder qua the Judgment Debtor and does not in terms, direct the Judgment Debtor to do or to refrain from doing any particular act or thing. Since there is no command issued to the Judgment Debtor to obey, the civil process cannot be issued for the compliance of that mandate or command. The decree- holder is free to seek his legal remedies by way of suit or otherwise on the basis of the declaration given in his favour..”.
judicial_order.annexed_proceedings: Ex. 1064 /2023 property is right of way reserved to the plaintiff. In view of clear grant of direction to removal of Sajja and Wall this executing court cannot direct removal of wall with pillar which is claimed to be existing in the year 2000 itself, as the entire building stands on the very said wall and pillar. As such the application is not maintainable and the same is hereby rejected. XXIV Addl.City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru

metadata.Case Title: SHAMANNA Y B vs SURESH B G
metadata.Court Name: PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Court Room & Judge: 15-CCH28 XIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 04/12/2023] I.A.No.1 filed by Decree holder seeking police help to break open the lock to execute the delivery warrant is hereby allowed. Issue delivery warrant with Police help. Issue Intimation to SHO, Bagalagunte Police station. Call on: 20.12.2023.
metadata.Order Procedural History: 1 EX.No.1130/2023 04.12.2023: ORDERS ON IA NO: 1 1. The applicant/DHR has filed I.A.No.1 under Section 151 of CPC seeking an order to break open the lock and hand over the vacant possession of the suit property with help of jurisdictional Police station for the reasons stated in the accompanying affidavit. 2. In the accompanying affidavit it is contended that OS no: 1306/2004, filed by the DHR for declaration and possession was decreed on 16.1.2015. RFA no: 381/2015, preferred by the Judgment debtors challenging the judgment and decree of civil suit has been dismissed on 18.5.2023. against, said order, the judgment debtors have preferred SLP no: 13461-2023 before Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, which came to be dismissed. The Judgment debtors have refused to handover the suit property to applicant, Dhr is a senior citizen who is aged about more than 75 years, and Jdrs have locked the door of the house. With these averments he prays to allow the petition. 2 EX.No.1130/2023 3. The opponents/Jdrs have filed objections, contending that the application is not maintainable. Dhr is seeking possession of the property, which is not terms of the decree passed by the court. The opponents are the purchasers of the property. 4. Heard the arguments of both the parties. Perused the material placed on record. 5. The suit was decreed on 16.01.2015, the decree is put in Execution Petition No.1130/2023, i.e., the present petition filed on 22.05.2023 to take possession of the property. In OS no: 1306/2004, the court decree the suit and directed the JDR to hand over the vacant possession of the suit property withing 3 months from the date of decree. Against said decree, the JDR has preferred RFA no: 381/2015 has been dismissed by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka on 18.5.2023. SLP no: 13461-2023, preferred by JDR has also dismissed by Hon’ble Supreme Court of India on 14.07.2023. 6. It is apparent that since 2015 till today, the JDR has not handed over the vacant possession of the suit premises to the applicants. The fruits of the decree is not realized by the decree
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: 3 EX.No.1130/2023 holder since 2015. The Bailiff of the court has submitted a report seeking police help to execute the Delivery Warrant alleging that JDRS have locked the suit property and obstructed the Bailiff while executing the delivery warrant. The applicant has made out sufficient ground to consider his plea. Hence following:- ORDER I.A.No.1 filed by Decree holder seeking police help to break open the lock to execute the delivery warrant is hereby allowed. Issue delivery warrant with Police help. Issue Intimation to SHO, Bagalagunte Police station. Call on: 20.12.2023. (Typed by the Presiding Officer, corrected, signed and then pronounced in the open court by me on 4th day of December, 2023) (SHAINEY K.M) XIV Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru.

judicial_order.procedural_history: 1 EX.No.1130/2023 04.12.2023: ORDERS ON IA NO: 1 1. The applicant/DHR has filed I.A.No.1 under Section 151 of CPC seeking an order to break open the lock and hand over the vacant possession of the suit property with help of jurisdictional Police station for the reasons stated in the accompanying affidavit. 2. In the accompanying affidavit it is contended that OS no: 1306/2004, filed by the DHR for declaration and possession was decreed on 16.1.2015. RFA no: 381/2015, preferred by the Judgment debtors challenging the judgment and decree of civil suit has been dismissed on 18.5.2023. against, said order, the judgment debtors have preferred SLP no: 13461-2023 before Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, which came to be dismissed. The Judgment debtors have refused to handover the suit property to applicant, Dhr is a senior citizen who is aged about more than 75 years, and Jdrs have locked the door of the house. With these averments he prays to allow the petition. 2 EX.No.1130/2023 3. The opponents/Jdrs have filed objections, contending that the application is not maintainable. Dhr is seeking possession of the property, which is not terms of the decree passed by the court. The opponents are the purchasers of the property. 4. Heard the arguments of both the parties. Perused the material placed on record. 5. The suit was decreed on 16.01.2015, the decree is put in Execution Petition No.1130/2023, i.e., the present petition filed on 22.05.2023 to take possession of the property. In OS no: 1306/2004, the court decree the suit and directed the JDR to hand over the vacant possession of the suit property withing 3 months from the date of decree. Against said decree, the JDR has preferred RFA no: 381/2015 has been dismissed by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka on 18.5.2023. SLP no: 13461-2023, preferred by JDR has also dismissed by Hon’ble Supreme Court of India on 14.07.2023. 6. It is apparent that since 2015 till today, the JDR has not handed over the vacant possession of the suit premises to the applicants. The fruits of the decree is not realized by the decree
judicial_order.judicial_findings: 3 EX.No.1130/2023 holder since 2015. The Bailiff of the court has submitted a report seeking police help to execute the Delivery Warrant alleging that JDRS have locked the suit property and obstructed the Bailiff while executing the delivery warrant. The applicant has made out sufficient ground to consider his plea. Hence following:- ORDER I.A.No.1 filed by Decree holder seeking police help to break open the lock to execute the delivery warrant is hereby allowed. Issue delivery warrant with Police help. Issue Intimation to SHO, Bagalagunte Police station. Call on: 20.12.2023. (Typed by the Presiding Officer, corrected, signed and then pronounced in the open court by me on 4th day of December, 2023) (SHAINEY K.M) XIV Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru.

metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 14/12/2024] Ex 1163/2023 The case is taken before this Lok Adalath for conciliation. D.Hr and J.Dr and their respective counsels are present. After conciliation, the parties to the execution petition have settled the matter before this Lok Adalath on the following terms. Both parties and their respective counsels have filed joint memo stating that the J.Dr has paid the entire decreetal amount and D.Hr has acknowledged the receipt of the amount and further submits that the decree is fully satisfied. hearings.business_text: L/c for the DHR submits that, the JDR no.2 and 3 have filed their objections opposing the petition on the ground that the DHR herein have got the exparte decree. Alleged that no court summons have been duly served on them. The JDR no.2 and 3 have come to know that, there is a decree from this court only when the DHR came along with the bailiff for executing the A/W/M. Considering the same, they have filed the petition u/o 9 R 13 of CPC, thus they have sought staying the Ex.petition. But this court in Misc 1177/24 was pleased to allow IA.No. 1 by staying the Judgment and decree with a condition to furnish the bank guarantee to the decreetal amount within 30 days from the date of order. The said 30 days expires on 20.04.2025, till then the jdrs have not complied the said condition imposed by this court, thus no stay is operating against the DHR herein, thus prays to issue A/W/M to attach the car of the JDR no.2. The Jdrs are remained absent, admittedly this court in Misc 1177/24 on 20.03.2025 by allowing IA.No. 1 was pleased to stay the Judgment and decree with a condition that JDR no.2 and 3 shall furnish the bank guarantee to the decreetal amount within 30 days, the said 30 days got expired on 20.04.2025. Further there is an order that, in the event of failure to comply the said order the stay order get canceled automatically. Admittedly the JDR no.2 and 3 have not complied the said order in Misc 1177/24, not even sought an extension of time to comply the same, by assigning the valid reasons, if that aspect is considered the JDRs have not made the grounds as to why the warrant for attaching their movables shall not be issued. Considering the same, this court felt, as the JDRs have not made out any grounds to not to execute the decree. Thus this court felt, if the prayer of the DHR is considered and order of A/W/M of the JDR no.2 is done, to recover the balance decreetal amount of Rs.10,04,823/- which is as per the MOC filed by the DHR. As the MOC filed by the DHR is also not disputed by the JDRs herein, thus ordered to issue A/W/M of the JDR no.2 to attaching his car no.KA 03 MT 9873 as per the B extract furnished by the DHR along with the PF memo. Directed the DHR to assist the bailiff to execute the A/W/M against the JDR no.2 to recover Rs.1004823/-. Call on 17-06-2025

metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 15/04/2026] EX 1190/2023 Counsel for DHR has filed process memo for issuance of cause notice to JDR at the same address as mentioned in the cause title despite office endorsement shows that ‘JDR has left the address’. The process filed today is rejected. It appears that DHR is not aware of the correct address of the JDR. In the light of the judgment of Apex court in Periyammal through L/Rs Vs Rajamani in Civil Appeal No. 3640-3642/2025 wherein the trial court have been directed to dispose of E.P. within a period of 6 months. Hence this court of the opinion that, the E.P. is required to be closed, with a liberty to the DHR to file fresh E.P. after tracing the address of JDR Accordingly, the above E.P. is closed with liberty to file fresh Petition after tracing the address of JDR. XLI Addl. CC & SJ

metadata.Case Title: M/s RADESHYAM LAMINATES AND DECORS PRIVATE LIMITED vs RAMA ENTERPRISES RAMANAGAR
metadata.Court Name: PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Court Room & Judge: 1003-CCH53 LII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Petitioner: M/s RADESHYAM LAMINATES AND DECORS PRIVATE LIMITED
metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 04/11/2023] The application filed by the Dhr U/s 39 R/w Sec.151 of CPC is hereby allowed. The office is hereby directed to transfer the decree dated 06.02.2023 passed by this court in O.S.740/2022 to the court of Learned Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ramanagar for execution of the said decree in accordance with law. Accordingly, this petition is closed before this court. LII ACC & SJ, B’luru.
metadata.Order Procedural History: EX 1207/2023 ORDERS ON IA.No.2/2023. Dhr has filed this application U/s 39 R/w Sec.151 of CPC praying to transfer the decree to the court of Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC, Ramanagar. It is stated in the affidavit filed in support of the application that Jdr is residing within the jurisdiction of this court and he is carrying on business within the jurisdiction of Learned Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ramanagar. Hence, the Dhr has prayed to transfer this petition to the court of Learned Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ramanagar for execution of decree. This petition is filed by the petitioner praying for execution of the money decree passed in O.S.740/2022 dated 06.02.2023. As per the said decree the defendant is held liable to pay sum of Rs.2,13,474/- to the plaintiff with interest. The plaintiff has sought for execution of the decree by way of attachment of movable properties of Jdr and by way of arrest of the Jdr. As per the address mentioned in the decree and as stated by the Dhr in the affidavit filed in support of the application, the Jdr is running business within the jurisdiction of the Ramanagar. As such the decree for recovery of money cannot be executed against the Jdr by way of attachment of the property of Jdr and by arresting him. Sec.39 of the CPC provides that if a person against whom the decree is passed actually and volunteerly resides or carries on business or personally work for gain within the local limits of jurisdiction of some other court, the court which passed the decree may on the application of the Dhr send it for execution to another court of competent jurisdiction. In this case, the Dhr himself has sought for transfer the decree to Ramanagar Court. Since, Jdr is residing within the local jurisdiction of Ramanagar and since he is carrying on the business in Ramanagar, I am of the opinion that, there is necessity of transferring the decree to court of Learned Prl.Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ramanagar in order to enable the decree holder to get the execution of the decree. Hence, I am of the opinion that, the application filed by the Dhr is deserves to be allowed. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:- ORDER The application filed by the Dhr U/s 39 R/w Sec.151 of CPC is hereby allowed. The office is hereby directed to transfer the decree dated 06.02.2023 passed by this court in O.S.740/2022 to the court of Learned Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ramanagar for execution of the said decree in accordance with law. Accordingly, this petition is closed before this court. LII ACC & SJ, B’luru.

judicial_order.procedural_history: EX 1207/2023 ORDERS ON IA.No.2/2023. Dhr has filed this application U/s 39 R/w Sec.151 of CPC praying to transfer the decree to the court of Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC, Ramanagar. It is stated in the affidavit filed in support of the application that Jdr is residing within the jurisdiction of this court and he is carrying on business within the jurisdiction of Learned Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ramanagar. Hence, the Dhr has prayed to transfer this petition to the court of Learned Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ramanagar for execution of decree. This petition is filed by the petitioner praying for execution of the money decree passed in O.S.740/2022 dated 06.02.2023. As per the said decree the defendant is held liable to pay sum of Rs.2,13,474/- to the plaintiff with interest. The plaintiff has sought for execution of the decree by way of attachment of movable properties of Jdr and by way of arrest of the Jdr. As per the address mentioned in the decree and as stated by the Dhr in the affidavit filed in support of the application, the Jdr is running business within the jurisdiction of the Ramanagar. As such the decree for recovery of money cannot be executed against the Jdr by way of attachment of the property of Jdr and by arresting him. Sec.39 of the CPC provides that if a person against whom the decree is passed actually and volunteerly resides or carries on business or personally work for gain within the local limits of jurisdiction of some other court, the court which passed the decree may on the application of the Dhr send it for execution to another court of competent jurisdiction. In this case, the Dhr himself has sought for transfer the decree to Ramanagar Court. Since, Jdr is residing within the local jurisdiction of Ramanagar and since he is carrying on the business in Ramanagar, I am of the opinion that, there is necessity of transferring the decree to court of Learned Prl.Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Ramanagar in order to enable the decree holder to get the execution of the decree. Hence, I am of the opinion that, the application filed by the Dhr is deserves to be allowed. As per the terms of compromise, the parties agreed to cancel the registered sale deed dated 14/3/2011 bearing No.08700/2010 -11 recorded in CD No.BSKD104 in the Sub Registrar of Banshankari and cancellation of sale deed dated 14/3/2011 bearing No. 8698/2010- 11 recorded in CD No.104 in the Office of the Sub Registrar, Banashankari. 2. The Decree Holder also produced certified copy of the compromised petition and certified copy of the order sheet dated 12/3/2022 which clearly reveals that, the parties in the suit entered into a compromise and agreed for the decree of the suit as per the terms of compromise petition. In the compromise petition dated 12/3/2022, the parties have clearly admitted to cancel the aforesaid sale deeds. Accordingly the court passed order stating that the suit is decreed as per the terms of compromise. The court has also drawn the decree accordingly. 3. There is no material on record to show that the said judgment and decree has been challenged or set aside Ex.1227/2023 or modified. Hence, it has to be accepted that the compromise decree has attained the finality. Hence, this execution petition to be allowed in directing the Sub Registrar to cancel the above said sale deeds. Hence the following: ORDERS The Senior Sub Registrar of Banashankari is hereby directed to cancel the two sale deeds dated 14/3/2011 bearing No. 08700/2010 -11 recorded in CD No.BSKD104 in the Sub Registrar of Banshankari and sale deed dated 14/3/2011 bearing No. 8698/2010-11 recorded in CD No.104 in the Office of the Sub Registrar, Banashankari after collecting necessary stamp duty or charges in accordance with law. Office to issue necessary intimation to the concerned sub registrar along with original sale deed produced in OS No. 2131/2011 for necessary endorsement. The Decree Holder is also liable to pay the required stamp duty or charges required for the cancellation of aforesaid two sale deeds. (PADMA PRASAD) XVIII Additional City Civil Judge, Bengaluru.

hearings.business_text: Case is called out. Decree-holder absent. Not complied office objections. Passed over. This is a petition based on award passed by the sold Arbitrator for recovery of amount. The office has raised objections for payment of deficit stamp duty of Rs.765/-. As per the judgment in WP No.29299/2013 dated 23-10-2024 in case of Mahindra and Mahendra Finance Service Limited v/s K V Chandrashekar and other. In para 20 of the judgment observed that award granting recovery of loans advanced does not qualify as an instrument chargeable under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act. In para 21 it obsered as follow: An arbitral award should not be subject to any stamp duty under the broad provisions of Section 3(b) when read with Sections 19(a) and (b) due to its unique intangible nature and legislative oversight, which distinguishes an award from other instruments enumerated in the schedule of the Act, which, if executed outside the State of Karnataka and then enforced in the State, would typically incur the stamp duty. And held that stamp duty cannot be subjected to award. The above said judgment is applicable to the case on hand, the facts are similar to that case. Accordingly, office objection is over ruled. Issue cause notice to Judgment Debtors No.1 to 3 through the process of court and by RPAD. Call on: 19-03-2025

hearings.business_text: Case is called out. Passed over. This is a petition based on award passed by the sold Arbitrator for recovery of amount. The office has raised objections for payment of deficit stamp duty of Rs.885/-. As per the judgment in WP No.29299/2013 dated 23-10-2024 in case of Mahindra and Mahendra Finance Service Limited v/s K V Chandrashekar and other. In para 20 of the judgment observed that award granting recovery of loans advanced does not qualify as an instrument chargeable under Article 11 of the Karnataka Stamp Act. In para 21 it obsered as follow: An arbitral award should not be subject to any stamp duty under the broad provisions of Section 3(b) when read with Sections 19(a) and (b) due to its unique intangible nature and legislative oversight, which distinguishes an award from other instruments enumerated in the schedule of the Act, which, if executed outside the State of Karnataka and then enforced in the State, would typically incur the stamp duty. And held that stamp duty cannot be subjected to award. The above said judgment is applicable to the case on hand, the facts are similar to that case. Accordingly, office objection is over ruled. Issue cause notice to Judgment Debtors No.1 and 2 through the process of court and by RPAD. Call on: 19-03-2025

hearings.business_text: Case called out. JDR No. 2 namely K.K. Shekar present and prays one month time for vacating the petition schedule properties. The order sheet discloses that JDR No.2 K.K.Shekar on 07.08.2023 filed affidavit stating that he has approached one sri.Kashinath who is a owner of house complex consisting of 4 floors at Yediyur circle, at TATA Silk Form, Bangalore and has agreed to lease out of 1st floor of one of the tenanted portion on monthly rental basis and he has also agreed to enter into a lease agreement within 20 days and thereafter he has agreed to hand over vacant possession of the 1st Floor unit and prayed one month time to vacate and hand over the vacant possession to the auction purchaser. Accordingly, after considering the said submission of JDR No.2, this court granted one month time to Jdr No.2 to vacate and surrender the vacant possession to the auction purchaser. In the said order dt. 07.08.2023 itself, the court made it clear that failure of JdR No.2 to vacate and hand over the possession, the court will passed order for issuance of delivery warrant as prayed in the execution petition in this date of hearing. In view of these facts the prayer of JDR No.2 K.K. Shekar to extend one month time to vacate and surrender the vacant possession of the premises of in his premises is hereby rejected. Consequently court proceed to pass the following; ORDER Issue delivery warrant of the petition schedule premises as prayed with the help of jurisdictional police and also with permission to break open the lock if put to the schedule premises and deliver the vacant possession to the decree holder/ auction purchaser on payment of required necessary process fee. metadata.Case Title: SBI CARDS AND PAYMENT SERVICES LTD vs M G RANGASWAMAIAH
metadata.Court Name: PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Court Room & Judge: 31-CCH31 XXX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
metadata.Petitioner: SBI CARDS AND PAYMENT SERVICES LTD
metadata.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 29/04/2026] Ex.Case No.1303/2023 3(a). It is submitted that, the judgments relied by the sole arbitrator are not applicable to the facts of the present case. Further there is no agreement entered between the DHr and JDr, thus, no breach of terms of agreement arises and sole arbitrator failed to prove the existence of credit card liability. The arbitral award does not specify details of date, month, year of issuance of credit card and there is no cause of action. Further submits that, the credit card facility was availed long back in 2004-2005 and not in 2022 and all the dues of SBI cards were already cleared through cheque to an authorized SBI cards officer, who assured to close the matter. The recovery proceedings initiated by the DHr is barred by limitation as the credit cards dates are way back in the year 2004-2005, while arbitration is initiated on 14.03.2022 after lapse of more than 18 years. The arbitral award is unconstitutional and cannot be enforced as there was no opportunities given to JDr to contest the proceedings and it is exparte award 5

hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The decree for delivery of possession and arrears of rent. The delivery warrant issued to the JDR returned unexecuted, on the ground that the petition schedule property is kept locked. In the petition itself the petitioner as sought an order to break open the lock of the petition schedule property and to deliver the same in favour of the DHR. By considering the same, ordered to issue delivery warrant to deliver the vacant petition schedule property in favour of the DHR herein. metadata.Order Procedural History: 1 Orders on IA.1 I.A. No.1 filed by the decree holder under Order 6 Rule 17 of CPC to amend the Execution Petition regarding the amounts stated in the Execution Petition in figures claiming that is typographical error. The said application is supported with the affidavit of decree holder. The JDr filed detailed objections. On that basis the point for consideration is as under: “Whether the decree holder made out sufficient grounds to amend the petition as prayed?” Heard the arguments. Perused the materials on records. My finding on the above point is in the affirmative, for the following: The main contention of the decree holder is that the decree holder is entitled to add interest @ 15% on Rs.1,61,037/-. But the said figure has been mentioned as Rs. 1,16,037/- instead of Rs.1,61,037/-. On perusal of the record, it appears to be 2 typographical error while mentioning the figure in the application. The objections raised by the JDr is treated as the objection to the main petition. The said contention to be decided during the course of execution of this petition. It is relevant to note that the JDr has also filed objections to the main petition. When the Court considering the said objections, certainly the Court can decide about the entitlement of decree holder for the amount claimed in the petition. When the decree holder made out a prima facie case regarding amendment claiming i.e., typographical error particularly stating that number 6 and 1 inter-changed while typing the said figure. As such, the said rectification can be allowed and even allowing of such rectification could not cause any hardship to the JDr as the JDr is liable to pay the amount deserves to be received by the decree holder as per award passed in the main case. Accordingly, this Court is of the humble opinion that the decree holder has made out sufficient grpounds to allow the IA No.1. Accordingly, the above point is answered in the affirmative and proceed to pass the
metadata.Order Judicial Findings: 3 following: ORDER IA No.1 filed under Order 6 Rule 17 of CPC by the decree holder is hereby allowed. Accordingly, the decree holder is permitted to amend the Execution Petition. For amendment and amended petition by 10.12.2024. (PADMA PRASAD) II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, & Spl. Judge, Bengaluru.

But the Plaintiff who is the DHR herein has filed the Petition and sought the direction of this court against the JDR/Defendant to remove the iron structures fixed in the common passage I.e, in “B” schedule property. Whatever he is claiming relief under the execution petition has not been granted either in the judgment or in the decree passed by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in RFA No.139/2016. In absence of such order, this court can’t go beyond the decree of the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka and proceed with this petition against the JDR, hence under these circumstances the petition does not survive for consideration and deserves to be dismissed and thereby the petition is dismissed. In view of the dismissal of the execution petition all pending IAs are disposed.

LVI ACC & SJ, Bengaluru.

In judgment passed by Honble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642 of 2025 in case of Peruyammal (Dead Through Lrs.) Vs V. Rajamani and another etc., dated 06.03.2025, it is held that, The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. In view of above said judgment, the decree holder has not taken effective steps. Sufficient time is given. There are no grounds to proceed further. This petition is dismissed for default and non prosecution. C/c XLIII ACC & SJ, Bengaluru.

In judgment passed by Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642 of 2025 in case of Peruyammal (Dead Through Lrs.) -Vs- V. metadata.Order Procedural History: EX 1475/2023 Case called before daily Lokadalath. Both the parties and their advocates are present. Both filed joint memo stating that the matter has been settled in between the parties. In view of the compromise Jdr No.1 and 4 have agreed to pay sum of Rs.7,00,000/- to the Dhr as the full and final settlement. In this regard Jdr No.1 and 4 have paid a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- by way of cash to the Decree Holder and Decree Holder acknowledged the receipt of the same. Further 2 cheques have been issued by the Jdr No.1 and 4 for Rs.1,50,000/- each dated 20.01.2027 and 20.03.2027 having No.011879 and No.011880 drawn on Karnataka Bank, Abbigere Branch, Bengaluru. If at all the cheques have not been encashed the Decree Holder has the right to proceed in accordance with the law. In view of the above terms of the compromise both the parties submitted that the execution petition may be closed. Heard. The terms of the joint memo are read over to the parties. They admit the compromise arrived in between the parties are genuine, voluntary, fair and without any force. In view of the above terms of the joint memo the above joint memo is taken on record. Accordingly, the above execution petition is dismissed in view of the terms of the joint memo. IX A.C.C. & S.J., Bengaluru.

metadata.Order Procedural History: Ex.No.1476/2023 The Decree Holder counsel filed execution petition for the recovery of amount of Rs.1,09,897/- in the dispute No.DRB/SZ/CFS/16/2011-12 dated 28.03.2013 passed by the Deputy Registrar of Chits South Zone, Chamarajapet, Bengaluru The Decree Holder prayed in the execution petition praying to transfer the decree for execution in that Court as JDRs are residing in the jurisdiction of Prl. Civil Judge Court at Chittoor, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh. As per section 39 of C.P.C. it says as follows : “39. Transfer of decree : (1) The Court which passed a decree may, on the application of the Decree Holder, send it for execution to another Court [of competent jurisdiction],- a) if the person against whom the decree is passed actually and voluntarily resides or carries on business, or personally works for gain, within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other Court, or b) if such person has no property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court which passed the decree sufficient to satisfy such decree and has Ex.No.1476/2023 property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other Court, or c) if the decree directs the sale or delivery of immovable property situate outside the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court which passed it, or d) if the Court which passed the decree considers for any other reason, which it shall record in writing, that the decree should be executed by such other Court. 2) The Court which passed a decree may of its own motion send it for execution to any subordinate Court of competent jurisdiction. 3) For the purposes of this section, a Court shall be deemed to be a Court of competent jurisdiction if, at the time of making the application for the transfer of decree to it, such Court would have jurisdiction to try the suit in which such decree was passed. 4) Nothing in this section shall be deemed to authorise the Court which passed a decree to execute such decree

As per the compromise decree parties have to agree to hand over the properties of their respective share within six months from the date of compromise. 7. Both the DHR and JDRs have to comply the compromise term No.7 in the compromise decree to get the fruits of compromise decree in respect of item No.1 and 2 petition properties. Item No.1 is residential house that should be divided by appointing a Court Commissioner. Without all these or without complying the terms of compromise decree both DHR and JDRS shall not get fruits of decree passed in the suit OS 1037/2017. hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: No representation on behalf of the DHR and counsel. On perusal of the petition as well as Judgment in O.S 7770/15 it reflects that, defendant is residing at Kannur, Kerala District. The suit filed by the JDR for recovery of sum of Rs.968755/- with interest at 24% P.A from the date of suit till the date of recovery of the suit claim. The suit ended in decree. On the strenght of Judgment and decree, first prayer in the Ex.petition for attachment and sale of movable of JDR and 2nd prayer is arrest of JDR, in the petition also the address of the JDR shown as residing at Sagarika, No.19-A/3, Wellesly raod, Baby beach road, Kannur Kerala District for execution of the suit claim. Considering the prayer in the petition it is very necessary to attach the movables of the JDR in the address where he is residing, but JDR is not residing in the Jurisdiction of court, even for arrest notice JDR is not residing in Jurisdiction of court, as per sec 39 of CPC the court which passed a decree holder send it for execution for another court for competent Jurisdiction. (a).if the person against whom the decree is passed actually and voluntarily resides or carries on business, or personally works for gain, within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other Court, or(b)if such person has not property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court which passed the decree sufficient to satisfy such decree and has property within the local limits of the jurisdiction of such other Court, or(c)if the decree directs the sale or delivery of immovable property situate outside the local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court which passed it, or(d)if the Court which passed the decree considers for any other reason, which it shall record in writing, that the decree should be executed by such other Court.(2)The Court which passed a decree may of its own motion send it for execution to any subordinate Court of competent jurisdiction.(3)[ For the purposes of this section, a Court shall be deemed to be a Court of competent jurisdiction if, at the time of making the application for the transfer of decree to it, such Court would have jurisdiction to try the suit in which such decree was passed.] [Inserted by the Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1976, Section 18 (w.e.f. 1.2.1977). ](4)[ Nothing in this section shall be deemed to authorise the Court which passed a decree to execute such decree against any person or property outside the local limits of its jurisdiction.] [Inserted by the Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1976, Section 2 (w.e.f. 1.7.2002). Sec 40-Where a decree is sent for execution in another State, it shall be sent to such Court and executed in such manner as may be prescribed by rules in force in that State. By virtue of sec 40 of CPC, directed the counsel for DHR to file necessary application for transfer of decree to the concerned Jurisdiction court at Kannur, Kerala State on next date of hearing without fail. Call on 30-08-2025

hearings.business_text: Counsel for Dhr present and filed memo stating that petition has been settled between the parties and therefore, Ex.P may be closed as fully satisfied. Jdr No.1 and Counsel for Jdrs present and submit despite the directions issued by this court the Dhr has not returned the original documents to Jdr No.1. The counsel for Dhr submit original documents were produced before the Deputy Registrar by the Dhr at the time of filing of petition in dispute No.DRB/TZ/CFS/148/ 2021-22 and therefore, the Jdr can obtain original documents from the Deputy Registrar. Counsel for Jdrs submit as the original documents were produced by Dhr before Deputy Registrar, the office of Deputy Registrar declined to return the documents to the custody of Jdrs. The court find substance in the submission of Counsel for Jdrs. More so, when the present execution petition is filed for enforcement of decree passed by the Deputy Registrar in the said case and the original documents are in the custody of Deputy Registrar and it was produced before Deputy Registrar by the Dhr and the Jdr No.1 satisfied the decree amount, it is obvious on the part of the Dhr to receive back the original documents from the Deputy Registrar and hand over the same to the Jdr No.1. Hence, Dhr is directed to receive back the documents from the office of the Deputy Registrar and hand over the same to Jdr No.1 along with Nil Encumbrance Certificate within 15 days and obtain acknowledgment from the Jdr No.1 or otherwise Jdr No.1 is at liberty to take legal action against Dhr. Subject to above direction to the Dhr, the petition is hereby closed as satisfied.

The decree is passed on 25.10.2022 directing the Jdr to pay a sum of Rs.1,45,000/- along with interest at the rate of 15 percent per annum along with the cost of Rs.14,800/-. The defence of the Jdr is that some amounts were paid on 07.10.2017, 17.10.2017, 24.10.2017, 02.11.2017, 16.11.2017, 24.11.2017, 01.12.2017, 26.07.2018, 02.01.2019, 27.08.2018, but the suit is filed on 16.10.2019. all the above payments were made prior to the institution of the suit. Therefore the payments yet to be made prior to the institution of the suit cannot be considered. It is an admitted fact that in the present execution petition a sum of Rs.50,000/- has paid on 07.06.2024 and a sum of Rs.25,000/- was paid on 21.08.2024 and another amount of Rs.25,000/- is paid on 11.09.2024. therefore the amount paid by the Jdr is only Rs.1Lakh. The Jdrs are liable to pay the remaining amount with interest. Therefore the memo filed by the Jdrs is rejected and the following orders are passed. ORDER Jdrs are directed to pay Rs.2,50,820/- due as on today on the next hearing date without fail. By 03.07.2025.

hearings.judge: CCH18 XIX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Decree Holder No.1 was hospitalized because of ill-health and was discharged recently and her presence is secured today through video conference wherein she has expressed her willingness for compromise. Other Decree Holders are present. Judgment Debtors (Judgment Debtor No.2 as General Power of Attorney holder of Judgment Debtor No.1) are present. Auction purchasers – Smt.Aruna.J and Sri Nishwanth.R, S/O.Raja Reddy are present. The Decree Holders and Judgment Debtors filed memo stating that they have successfully executed registered Sale Deed on 07.06.2024 in favour of purchasers Smt.Aruna.J and Sri Nishwanth.R, thereby absolutely conveying petition schedule property for total sale consideration of Rs.1,56,00,000/- (One crore fifty six lakh only). After deducting all the expenditure out of total sale consideration it will come to Rs.1,49,19,000/- which is deposited to the Court. Now they are entitled for their respective share proceeds as per preliminary decree passed in O.S.No.1341/2015 and final decree passed in FDP.99/2021 i.e. 1/9th share each. Out of the said amount of Rs.1,49,19,000/-, Decree Holders and Judgment Debtors are entitled as stated in the memo. Hence, it is prayed to release the same to their respective Bank accounts. Records reveal that sum of Rs.1,49,19,000/- is deposited by the auction purchaser to the court out of which sum of Rs.60,00,000/- is kept as Fixed Deposit in Karnataka Bank Ltd., vide order dated 02.03.2024. The office note shows that a sum of Rs.89,19,000/- is in CCD and an amount of Rs.60,42,000/- received from Karnataka Bank F.D. and sent the same to S.B.I. for clearance but R.O. challen has not yet returned. Auction purchasers /their counsel present and submitted no objection to release the amount in favour of Decree Holders and Judgment Debtors. In view of the same Joint memo filed by both Decree Holders and Judgment Debtors is accepted and execution petition is closed as fully satisfied. Decree Holders and Judgment Debtors have produced affidavit, cancelled cheque, vouchers, Bank account details, Aadhar Card and PAN Card. In view of the same, office is hereby directed to release the amount to the Decree Holders and Judgment Debtors through K-2 to their respective accounts as stated in the Joint memo after credit of F.D. Rs.60,42,000/- to CCD on proper identification of the parties through their advocates as per law.

This court of the opinion that, the E.P. is required to be closed, with a liberty to the DHR to file fresh E.P. if permissible under law Accordingly, the above E.P. is closed.

hearings.judge: CCH30 XXIX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: ORDERS ON MAINTAINABILITY The D.H.R has filed the present petition to execute the decree passed in O.S. No.3279/2009. The said suit was decreed on 06.12.2010. The present petition was filed on 24.07.2023. It shows that the present petition is filed after lapse of 12 years 7 months and 18 days. As per Article 136 of Limitation Act, the execution petition has to be filed within 12 years from the date of decree enforceable. As per the judgment and decree passed in O.S. No. 3279/2009, the decree can be enforceable from 07.03.2010. But the D.H.R has not filed the present petition within the period of limitation, therefore the decree passed in O.S. No.3279/2009 cannot be executed. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed as barred by limitation.

Counsel for the Judgment debtor submitted that, all further proceedings of execution No.1926/2023 is stayed subject to the Judgment debtor depositing a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- before this court. As Judgment debtor has already deposited a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- on 11-01-2024, Decree holder is not entitled to proceed with this execution petition. On other hand Ld. Counsel for the Decree holder took this court through the orders dated 13-12-2023 passed by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru in RFA No.2351/2023 which reads as under. “In the meanwhile, interim order dated 06.12.2023 is stayed, subject to the appellant depositing a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- before the Executing court on or before 12.01.2024”. A careful reading of both the orders dated 06-12-2023 and 13-12-2023, it is clear that Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru vide order dated 06-12-2023 stayed the further proceedings of this execution petition till next date of hearing. Further through order dated 13-12-2023, said interim order dated 06-12-2023 is stayed. Moreover, there is no further extension of interim order dated 06-12-2023. Hence, there is no impediment to proceed with this execution petition. Ld. Counsel for the Judgment debtor prays time to file objections to I.A.No.I. hearings.business_text: I.A.No.1 filed u/or 21 R 35 of C.P.C. by the DHR to issue delivery warrant and direct the Judgment-Debtor to hand over the possession of the suit schedule property to the Decree-Holder in the interest of justice and equity. It is contended in the affidavit accompanying application that Decree-Holder had filed O.S.6735/2014 against the Judgment-Debtor for the relief of Declaration and Delivery of possession. The said suit so filed by the DHR came to be decreed vide judgment and decree dated:04.03.2023, but the JDR has failed to delivery vacant possession of the suit schedule property. Hence, the present application. Though notice was issued and the same is served on the JDR, he failed to appear before the court. As per order 21 R 35 of C.P.C. where a decree is for the delivery of any immovable property, possession thereof shall be delivered to the party by issuing delivery warrant. Hence, the application filed by the DHR is hereby allowed. Office is directed to issue delivery warrant in the prescribed format to hand over the possession of the suit schedule property to the DHR in accordance with law in terms of the decree. Await report, by 20.02.2024.

hearings.judge: CCH32 XX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Perused the petition and the records and I.A No.I/24. After perusal of the records, it is found that J.Dr neither residing nor running her business within the jurisdiction of this court. The records further reveals that J.Dr is also not having any movable or immovable property/ies within the jurisdiction of this court. When J.Dr is not residing or not running her business or not working for gain within jurisdiction of this court and when she is also not having any kind of property within the jurisdiction of this court, the execution of the decree by this court is not possible. Hence, the decree requires to be transferred to the court in whose jurisdiction the J.Dr is actually residing or running her business or working for gain. Therefore, I proceed to pass the following ORDER Office is hereby directed to transfer the decree, a certificate (as stated in Rule 6 of Order XXI CPC) and related records to the jurisdictional court i.e Hon\''ble Principal Senior Civil Judge at Mysore for execution of decree, if PF is paid. And further directed to put up the file after receipt of the report from the executing court.

hearings.judge: CCH28 XIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Orders on I.A.No.1 1. The Learned counsel for decree holder has filed the instant application u/Sec.39 of CPC seeking transfer of Decree to Prl. Senior Civil Judge, Mysore to execute the decree as Judgment Debtor is residing and carrying out its business within the jurisdiction of aforesaid court. 2. Learned counsel for Decree Holder submitted that, judgment debtors resides and personally works for gain within the jurisdiction of above Court and therefore he prays for transfer of Decree. 3. Sec.39 of CPC enables the court which passed the decree send the decree to another court of competent jurisdiction for execution. Sec.39(a) of CPC enables the court which passed the decree may of its own motion send it for execution to any subordinate court of competent jurisdiction. The cause title of the Execution Petition and decree passed in OS No.1627/2014, reveals that JDR is in Vijayanagara Mysore. It is submittd that J.dr has not yet, deposited the award amount. Hence, following :: ORDER :: Acting U/Sec. 39(a) of CPC, the application filed by the Dhr u/Sec.151 of CPC is hereby allowed and the decree is hereby transfered to Prl. Senior Civil Judge, Mysore for execution of decree passed in OS No.1627/2014. Office to send the records to above court as per law. Issue DTC.
