hearings.business_text: I.A. No.13 is filed by the JDR No.1 u/Sec. 151 of CPC., for an order to keep in abeyance of auction sale dated 09.09.2025. The counsel for the DHR has filed the detail objections to the application contending that the present application is filed on behalf of the JDR No.1 by an advocate who has not filed any vakalath on behalf of JDR No.1 or authorized to file an application and further the affidavit in support of application by JDR No.2 in her individual capacity but not as a representative of JDR No.1. hence, the application is liable to be dismissed. Even as per the documents furnished by the JDR only two movables are hypotheticated to the bank and the said movable assets are entirely different from the assets attached and auctioned by this Court. The JDRs have removed all their assets from the suit schedule premises to some unknown place before delivery of possession of the suit schedule premises to the DHR. It is further contended that the JDRs are yet to pay Rs.2,19,44,550/- and even they have not filed memo of calculation. The JDR has sought for stay of auction sale dated 09.09.2025 till furnishing the details of the payments made by them. According to the DHR even half of the decreetal amount is not paid so far. Admittedly, auction sale was conducted on 09.09.2025 and entire sale price was deposited by the purchasers. As rightly contended by the DHR, the present application is filed only to protract the proceedings to see that the fruits of the decree is not enjoyed by the DHR. It is pertinent to have a glance at the ruling of Hon’ble supreme Court reported in the case of Periyammal (dead) through Lrs and other V/s V.Rajamani and another (Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025 dated 06.03.2025) wherein by reiterating the directions in the Rahul Sha’s case it is held that the execution petitions shall be disposed off at the earliest and preferably within the period of 6 months from the date of institution. The JDR has not made out any grounds to consider the application. Hence, the application is hereby dismissed on cost of Rs.500/- payable to the DHR. Issue delivery warrant as per the order dated 19.09.2025 if the entire sale price is deposited in the Court. Call on 15.10.2025

hearings.judge: CCH45 XLIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The counsel for JDR No.2 files application u/O 17 R 1 r/w/sec. 151 of CPC., seeking adjournment along with memo and photocopies of documents. The counsel for the DHR strongly objects to grant any adjournment on the ground that the auction purchasers have deposited entire sale price and therefore, the sale has become absolute and accordingly, he prays to issue delivery warrant. The execution petition is of the year 2023. The counsel for the DHR has placed reliance on the ruling of Hon’ble supreme Court reported in the case of Periyammal (dead) through Lrs and other V/s V.Rajamani and another (Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025 dated 06.03.2025) wherein by retreating the directions in the Rahul Sha’s case it is held that the execution petitions shall be disposed off at the earliest and preferably within the period of 6 months from the date of institution. Though the Petition is of the year 2023, the present application seeking adjournment is filed only in order to protract the proceedings. Thus preventing the DHR from enjoying the fruits of the Decree. In view of the ruling of the Hon’ble Supreme Court cited supra, the application filed by the JDR No.2 seeking adjournment is hereby rejected and the arguments of the JDR on I.A. No.13 is taken as nil. For Orders on I.A. No.13 by 26.09.2025

Rajamani and another etc., dated 06.03.2025, it is held that, The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. In view of above said judgment, the decree holder has not taken effective steps. There are no grounds to proceed further. PF is rejected. Hence, this petition is dismissed for default and non prosecution.

The D.Hr and J.Dr have entered into settlement before lok adalath and has settled the appeal by filing the memo of settlement before the lok adalath dated 03.11.2022 before this court and agreed to pay a sum of Rs.12,50,000/- in four installments on or before 30.06.2022. The J.Dr / accused was acquitted by order dated 03.11.2022. The D.Hr in execution of said amount has filed the execution petition No.2143/2023 for an of Rs.13,55,000/- along with interest at the rate 12% per annum and litigation expenses. The D.Hr has filed the present application to transfer the execution petition to be executed before the Senior Civil Judge, Magadi stating that the J.Dr has having movable and immovable property and his place of residence is Balenahalli Village, Madabal Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara. Hence the D.Hr prays to transfer the execution petition as prayed in the application. Heard, IA No.1 is allowed. Office is directed to transfer the execution petition to the Senior Civil Judge, Magadi as per law.

hearings.business_text: Perused the records and Execution petition and certified copy of judgment and decree passed by this court in OS.No.2838/2017, dtd. 20.06.2023. On perusal of records which reveals that the counsel for DHR had filed I.A.No.2 U/o 21 R 30 of CPC seeking an order for payment of decreetal amount. Accordingly, this court has passed an order dtd. 07.12.2023 and allowed the said application and directed the office to issue intimation to the custodian of the amount deposited by the auction purchaser in Ex.P.3193/2017 payable to the DHR in this case by the JDR and to file the compliance report. Subsequently as per the letter No. CCH 90-1/2024, dtd. 02.01.2024 the Sr. Sheristedar of City Civil Court (Commercial Courts Unit), Bengaluru has sent letter of intimation stating that the total sum of Rs.30,16,000/- has been transferred from Com.Ex.No.3193/2017 for payment in Ex.P.2156/2023 on the file of this CCH-39. As per the shara and note of the Sheristedar(Accounts), City Civil Court, Bengaluru dtd. 22.02.2024 a sum of Rs.30,16,000/- which was deposited in Com.Ex.No.3193/2017 as been transferred to this Ex.P.2156/2023. Hence, the said amount of Rs.30,16,000/- which has been transferred from Com. Ex.No.3193/2017 is available in the present Ex.No.2156/2023. Hence, office is directed to release a sum of Rs.30,16,000/- in favour DHR in accordance with Law. Further office is directed to file the compliance report by 07.06.2024.

hearings.judge: CCH26 X ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The Learned counsel appearing for the Dhr submitted that by virtue of Order 21 Rule 48 CPC if the Jdr is a government servant the execuytion petition can be filed before this court. He submitted that he would submit in detail later. Call later. Case called at 400pm. The Dhr and its counsel are absent. No representation. Examined the records. The Jdrs are the residents out side the limits of this court. Order 21 Rule 48 CPC merely provides that if the Jdr is a salaried person the court can attach a salary even if the Jdr or the disbursing officer is or is not within the local limits of the courts jurisdiction. The jurisdiction of the civil court is governed by Sec.15 to 20 of CPC and not U/o 21 Rule 48 CPC. In other words the suit or execution petition shall be executed in accordance with Sec.15 to 20 CPC and when the execution petition so executed if the Jdr or the disbursing officer is residing or working outside the limits of the court, then also the court can attach the salary. Therefore this contention of the Dhr is misconceived and cannot be accepted. The Dhr shall submit its arguments if any without fail by next hearing date. By 18.12.2024.

hearings.business_text: Case advanced. The counsel for Dhr files I.A.No.1 U/o 21 Rule 35(3) CPC seeking police production in execution of warrant and I.A.No.2 under the same provision seeking leave to the court officer to break open the lock of the schedule premises. Heard on IAs. This court has issued delivery warrant despiting with the issuance of notice to the Jdr as the EP has been filed within 2 years of the decree. Perused the report of the bailiff who has also reported that there was obstruction from the Jdr during the execution of warrant and therefore he has also sought for police protection. Perused the grounds urged in the IA which are justifiable one. Since the Jdr has obstructed the execution of warrant, in the interest of justice I.A.No.1 & 2 are allowed. Under I.A.No.1 issue direction to the concerned jurisdictional police to provide assistance to the court bailiff to execute the warrant as prayed for. Under I.A.No.2 the court bailiff/official is permitted/ directed to break open the lock of the schedule premises as prayed for. PF is paid. Await report by 08.12.2023.

hearings.judge: CCH26 X ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The counsel for Dhr submitted on memo dtd.16.09.2023. Under this memo the Dhr has stated that he was required to take court fee on the claim of arrears of rent sought for in the petition, but however he would not press for the said relief and he would maintain his claim for recovery of possession of the schedule property. Accordingly he has sought for liberty to seek for recovery of arrears of rent and future interest at the later stage and he would pay court fee at the time of seeking such reliefs and has accordingly sought for issue of delivery warrant. However in para 9 of the memo and also in the prayer column It is stated that the decree holder would withdraw the relief for recovery of future rent, maintenance and interest granted in the decree with a liberty to file fresh EP for recovery of the future rent maintenance and interest amount. However he has sought for recovery of rent from May 2018 till June 2019 and maintenance charges from 01.04.2017 to 27.08.2019. Since the office objections have been raised with regard to the claim of future rent and interest and the same has been waved off by the Dhr in the present petition, the memo is accepted. Since the EP has been filed within 2 years of date of decree, issue delivery warrant against the JDr as sought for. R/by 08.12.2023.

hearings.business_text: The Counsel for decree-holder is present and prays time. In judgment passed by Honble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642 of 2025 in case of Peruyammal (Dead Through Lrs.) -Vs- V. Rajamani and another etc., dated 06.03.2025, it is held that,The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. In view of above said judgment, the decree holder has not taken effective steps. Prayer of Counsel for decree-holder is rejected. There are no grounds to proceed further. Hence, this petition is dismissed for default and non prosecution.

hearings.business_text: DHR and JDR counsel are present. JDR counsel prays time for 15 days to settle the matter, DHR counsel submitted that no such settlement offered by the JDR. Hence, prayer of the JDR counsel is hereby rejected. Heard on the application filed U/Sec.151 of CPC, seeking police protection to execute attachment warrant of movables. On perusal of the record it appears that the Hon\\\''ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru, in its order dated.01.02.2024 was pleased to directed the JDR to furnish Bank guarantee for Rs.7,00,000/- within a period of 4 weeks. Inspite of such order the JDR has not complied with, therefore, this court has no other option, except the execute the Decree. Apart from this it is worth to note that the bailiff submitted his report stating that the JDR is causing obstruction for executing the attachment warrant. By considering the report submitted by the bailiff, I feel it is necessary to direct the concerned Police to give necessary protection for the time of executing attachment warrant of movables as per the list. hearings.business_text: Case taken on board on application filed by the counsel for the DHR. Counsel for the DHR files I.A.No.1 u/Sec.151 of C.P.C. for issuance of delivery of warrant by break opening lock of the schedule premises. It is contended in the affidavit accompanying application that the DHR is a senior citizen aged about 85 years and the judgment debtor is avoiding cause notice. It is further contended that the execution petition is filed within two years as required u/Or 21 R 22 of C.P.C. and issuance of cause notice is not mandatory. As could be seen from the records, though cause notice was issued to the JDR the same is returned unserved with shara door locked and addressee left, which go to show that the JDR is intentionally avoiding the cause notice. Hence, I.A.No.1 filed by DHR is hereby allowed. Issue delivery warrant in the prescribed form as prayed for in the application with a direction to break open the lock of the schedule premises with the aid of the police, if required, by 23.01.2024.

Rajamani and another etc., dated 06.03.2025, it is held that, The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. In view of above said judgment, the decree holder has not taken effective steps. There are no grounds to proceed further. Hence, this petition for default and non-prosecution.

hearings.business_text: ORDER I.A. No.1 filed by DHR U/O 21 Rule 43 of CPC seeking to issue attachment warrant of movables of JDR by break open lock with police help and grant such other order as just under circumstances of the case. On perusal of order sheet dated 28-09-2024 it is noted as the attachment warrant of movables issued prior to this application was failed to execute due to obstruction by JDR. If this application is allowed with direction to concerned jurisdictional police station to give police aid to execute the attachment warrant of movables by breaking open the lock to the premises of JDR with peaceful manner without disturbing system in the soceity and General public in the locality will not make hardship to other side. Accordingly, this Court proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A. No.1 filed by the DHR U/O 21 Rule 43 of CPC is hereby allowed. Accordingly, office is hereby directed to Issue attachment warrant of movables of JDRs if PF paid. The Counsel for DHR directed give details of jurisdictional police to give aid while executing the attachment warrant. Accordingly, the jurisdictional police is hereby directed to execute the same with peaceful manner without disturbing system in the soceity and General public in the locality. Issue attachment warrant of movables as per above Order. Call on 13-12-2024.

hearings.judge: CCH35 XXXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. Upon perusal of order sheet, it is noticed that, on the earlier dates of hearing, the counsel for DHR was directed to take steps against JDR for the issuance of attachment warrant of movables. Despite providing multiple opportunities, the DHR has failed to take proper steps against Jdr in order to effectively execute the decree. In view of the judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs & Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani & Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025 and in compliance of the circular No.2/2025 dated 01.04.2025 issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka mandating the disposal of execution petitions within 6 months, this Court is duty bound to prevent undue pendency of the execution petitions. Since the DHR has not diligently pursued the execution and no purpose would be served in keeping the petition pending further, the execution petition deserves to be disposed of. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification.

hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on the limitation. In this case the DHR has got the decree for recovery of money on 02.08.2010. The 12 yrs limitations to file the executing the decree will expires on 02.08.2022. But this petition being filed before this court on 26.09.2023, which is after lapse of more than 1 yr, 1 month 24 days. But L/c for the DHR submits that, the Hon\''ble Apex court in its sue moto WP(C) no.3/20 and Misc application no.21/22 , vide its order dt 10.01.2022 excluded the period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022 for the purpose of limitation. Thus he contended that, the said period is requires to be added to the remaining period commences from 01.03.2022 to file the petition. According to him as on 01.03.2022 the DHR has the 5 months 1 day time to file the petition, for which the saved period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022, which comes of 1 yr, 1 month 24 days are requires to be added to the 5 months 1 day, the total period available to the DHR to file petition is 1 yrs 6 months 24 days from 01.03.2022, said period will expires on 25.09.2023. As the petition is filed on 26.09.2023, the said petition is well in time. The contention of the DHR is cannot be accepted for the simple reason that, the Hon\''ble Apex court by considering the gravity of the Covid break down in the country was pleased to exclude the period btw 15.03.2020 to 28.02.2022 in the event if the limitation expired btw that period or limitation commences, in any of the circumstances the Hon\''ble Apex court hold that, 90 days period is available from 01.03.2022. If the remaining period of limitation is exceeding the 90 days in that event the longer period is going to be applied. If the said aspect are considered, the case of the DHR will not fall in any of the conditions. In fact the limitations to file the present petition was not expired btw the period excluded for the purpose of limitation by the Hon\''ble Apex court. In fact the DHR was having 5 months 1 day period from 01.03.2022 to file their petition, which expires on 01.09.2022 in that event the DHR should have been filed the present petition on or before 01.09.2022, as the present petition is filed after expiry of the limitation period, thus petition do not survives for the execution. Thus this petition is dismissed as it time barred decree.

hearings.business_text: ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ಪರ ವಕೀಲರು ಮಾನ್ಯ ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯಕ್ಕೆ ಮಧ್ಯಂತರ ಅರ್ಜಿ 2 ಸಿವಿಲ್ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯಾ ಸಂಹಿತೆ ಆಜ್ಞೆ 26 ನಿಯಮ 9 ಸಹ ಕಲಂ 151 ರಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅರ್ಜಿ ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಪತ್ರ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿ, ದಾವಾ ಆಸ್ತಿಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಪಟ್ಟಂತೆ ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ರವರು ಹಾಜರುಪಡಿಸಿದ ಕರಡು ಕ್ರಯಪತ್ರದ ಆಧಾರದ ಮೇಲೆ ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ರವರಿಗೆ ನೋಂದಣಿ ಕ್ರಯಪತ್ರ ಮಾಡಿಸಲು ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯದಿಂದ ಆಯುಕ್ತರನ್ನು ನೇಮಕ ಮಾಡಬೇಕೆಂದು ವಿನಂತಿಸಿಕೊಂಡಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಪ್ರಮಾಣಪತ್ರ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಲಾಗಿ, ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ರವರು ಡಿಕ್ರಿಯ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ದಾವಾ ಆಸ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ನೋಂದಣಿ ಕ್ರ‍‍ಯಪತ್ರ ಮಾಡಿಸಲು 13-12-2023 ರಂದು ಕರಡು ಕ್ರಯಪತ್ರವನ್ನು ಹಾಜರುಪಡಿಸಿದ್ದು, ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯದ ಸಿಬ್ಬಂದಿ ವರ್ಗದವರು ಕರಡು ಕ್ರಯಪತ್ರ ಸರಿ ಇರುತ್ತದೆ ಅಂತ ಹಿಂಬರಹ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಡಿಡಿ ಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಮೂದಿಸಿದ ಹಣ ಇನ್ನೂ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಜಮಾ ಆಗಿರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ ಅಂತ ತಿಳಿಸಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಅರ್ಜಿ, ಪ್ರಮಾಣಪತ್ರ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಲಾಗಿ, ಸಕಾರಣಗಳಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿರುವುದರಿಂದ, ಈ ಕೆಳಗಿನಂತೆಃ ಆದೇಶ ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ಪರ ವಕೀಲರು ಮಾನ್ಯ ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸಲ್ಲಿಸಿದ ಮಧ್ಯಂತರ ಅರ್ಜಿ 2ನ್ನು ಪುರಸ್ಕರಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ದಾವಾ ಅಸ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ರವರಿಗೆ ನೋಂದಣಿ ಕ್ರಯಪತ್ರ ಮಾಡಿಸಿಕೊಡುವ ಸಲುವಾಗಿ ದಿನಾಂಕಃ 13-12-2023 ರಂದು ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ರವರು ಹಾಜರುಪಡಿಸಿದ ಕರಡು ಕ್ರಯಪತ್ರದ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಆಯುಕ್ತರು ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ರವರಿಗೆ ಉಪ ನೋಂದಣಾಧಿಕಾರಿ ಕಚೇರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ನೋಂದಣಿ ಕ್ರಯಪತ್ರ ಮಾಡಿಸಲು ಶ್ರೀ ಎಂ.ಡಿ.ಯೆಾೕಗಾನಂದ ರಾಜು, ವಕೀಲರು, ಕೆೆಎಆರ್ ಸಂ.3538/2005, ಸಂ.3/3, 1ನೇ ಮಹಡಿ, 3ನೇ ಅಡ್ಡರಸ್ತೆ, ನೆಹರು ನಗರ, ಶೇಷಾದ್ರಿಪುರಂ, ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಇವರನ್ನು ನ್ಯಾಯಾಲಯದ ಆಯುಕ್ತರನ್ನಾಗಿ ನೇಮಕ ಮಾಡಲಾಯಿತು. ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ಆಯುಕ್ತರ ಶುಲ್ಕ ರೂ.5,000/- ಹಣವನ್ನು ಠೇವಣಿ ಇಡತಕ್ಕದ್ದು. ಡಿಹೆಚ್ಆರ್ ದಿನಾಂಕಃ 13-12-2023 ರಂದು ಹಾಜರುಪಡಿಸಿದ ರೂ.5,80,000/- ಹಣದ ಡಿಡಿ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಜಮಾ ಆದ ನಂತರ ಆಯುಕ್ತರಿಗೆ ವಾರೆಂಟ್‍ ಕಳುಹಿಸಲು ಆದೇಶಿಸಲಾಯಿತು. ಮುಂದಿನ ದಿನಾಂಕಃ 24-01-2024.

hearings.business_text: PF paid. Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on the office objection. The office has raised 2 objections firstly, showing the entry on the WP 23465/17 showing to be pending on 16.06.2022. as the suit itself got disposed off, the pendency of WP 23465/17 do not come in the way of executing the decree, for the reason that, the JDRs herein seems to be challenged the order of this court passed on application filed u/o 10 of CPC for staying this suit, alleging that there are other suits are pending. And also raised an objection with regard to the mode of calculation to claim the decreetal amount is not shown. But the DHR files the memo stating that, in the decree Rs.18000/- towards the arrears of rent has been awarded but the DHR herein have wrongly awarded but the DHR submits that she will not press on the arrears of rents and would wants to maintain this petition only for delivery of possession. By considering the same, memo is hereby allowed, petition for seeking arrears of rent is hereby dismissed as not pressed. Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on IA.No. 1, under which the DHR is seeking an order to delivery warrant to deliver the decreetal schedule property in favour of DHR. The DHR submits that, against the Judgment and decree of this court the JDRs have not preferred any appeal, thus no stay is operating on the Judgment and decree of this court. By considering the same, IA.No. 1 is hereby allowed, as the DHR has got the decree for ejecting the JDRs from the decreetal schedule property, thus ordered to issue delivery warrant to deliver the vacant possession of the decreetal schedule property in favour of the DHR by ejecting the JDRs. Call on 15.02.2024

hearings.business_text: No representation is made. In judgment passed by Honble Supreme Court of India in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642 of 2025 in case of Peruyammal (Dead Through Lrs.) -Vs- V. Rajamani and another etc., dated 06.03.2025, it is held that, The executing court must dispose of the execution proceedings within six months from the date of filing, which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay. hearings.business_text: Court sale is not conducted. Judgment-Debtor No.5 filed objections. Perused the same. Judgment-Debtor No.5 is jointly and severally liable to repay the award amount and hence, cannot say that without taking any action against Judgment-Debtor No.1 and 2 decree cannot proceed against him. Since award is jointly and severally executed, it is for the Decree-Holder to take steps against all of the Judgment-Debtor or any one of the Judgment-Debtor. Therefore there is no merits in the objections filed by Judgment-Debtor No.5 stating that the application is to be rejected. Already this court has ordered for sale of property belonging to Judgment-Debtor No.5 and hence, it is necessary to Re-issue sale proclamation and sale warrant. Accordingly the sale proclamation and sale warrant are reissued by rejecting the objections raised by Judgment-Debtor No.5. Spot sale, by 24.02.2025. Court sale, by 06.03.2025.

hearings.business_text: Case called. Both the Counsels present. DHR present. The Son of JDR named Ramesh present. The key of suit schedule premises handed over to DHR. In view of handing over of key the Counsel for JDR filed a memo about handing over the key. Memo taken on record. The Counsel for DHR files memo in view of handing over of the key stating that the E.P. is duly complied. Hence, memo is allowed. E.P. is hereby closed as fully satisfied.

hearings.judge: CCH12 XVI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called. Counsel for DHR advanced the matter to today\''s board and filed I.A. U/S 151 of CPC seeking direction to jurisdictional police to assist DHR in enforcing / implimenting and break open the lock of the premises to comply order dated 30-03-2024. Heard. Perused materials on record. In accompanying affidavit to the I.A. it is stated that this Court issued delivery warrant against JDR on 30-03-2024 directing the JDR to hand over the possession of the schedule premises. Further on 22-04-2024 when the Bailief and DHR attempted to execute delivery warrant the JDR physically obstructed them from doing so. Hence, for executing the said order this DHR prayed for police aid and filed this application. If this application is allowed with direction to the jurisdictional police station Upparpet mentioned in I.A. that to assist the DHR and Bailief to implement Order dated 30-03-2024 with peaceful manner without making any obstruction to public order will leads to justice. Hence, this court proceed to pass the following ORDER I.A. is allowed, the jurisdictional police mentioned in I.A. is hereby directed to give aid to implement order dated 30-03-2024. Re-issue Delivery warrant if PF paid. Call on 29-06-2024.

CCH5 IX ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: ORDERS On 20.04.2024 counsel for the JDR filed an application under Order 21 read with section 151 of CPC contending that, this Court has no jurisdiction to entertain the above execution petition. The application is supported by the affidavit of the JDR wherein he contended that, the execution petition has been filed for the recovery of the amount to the tune of Rs.36,28,544/- as per the order of the Court dated 12.07.2023 in O.S.No.1537/2021. Since DHR seeking the arrears of amount for more than Rs.3 lakhs the suit falls under the category Commercial dispute and the same is to be adjudicated by the designated Commercial Court. Accordingly, prayed to allow the application in the ends of the justice. In support of the submissions of the JDR, he has produced the decision of Hon’ble Punjab and Haryana High Court in Civil Revision No.2481/2019 wherein it was held that, the remedy is not to seek the rejection of the plaint, but for the transfer by moving an application before Commercial Appellate Division Bench of the High Court. The same was upheld by the different High Courts in many other cases. What is to be looked into is whether the dispute is a Commercial dispute in order to transfer the same. Here, even in the execution petition the arrears of rent claimed by the DHR is more than Rs.35 lakhs. Therefore, this Court is not having any jurisdiction to entertain the same. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following : O R D E R Office is hereby directed to place the above case before the Court Hon’ble Prl. District & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru for the necessary orders. Call on

hearings.business_text: Case is called out. Learned Counsel for Decree-holders filed memo of calculation and list of two documents. Heard the Learned Counsel for Decree-holder on IA No.3 and perused the materials on record. Plaintiffs have filed suit against the Defendants bearing OS No.1654/2022 seeking the relief of specific performance of contract. The plaintiffs and Defendants entered into compromise and the plaintiffs and Defendants agreed for sale consideration of Rs.2,28,50,000/- and at the time of sale agreement, plaintiffs paid Rs.56,40,652/- through NEFT/RTGS and this fact is admitted in para No.2 of compromise petition. As per the terms of compromise petition the Defendants agreed to execute the registered sale deed within 2 months after clearing loan amount of Rs.1,46,41,446/-. In para 7 of compromise petition, plaintiffs agreed to pay Rs..15 Lakhs after borrowing loan from any bank and clearing loan amount borrowed by the Defendants and the plaintiffs agreed to pay said amount of Rs.15 Lakhs to the Defendants through demand draft. On careful perusal of court sale deed the Defendants already received advance sale consideration of Rs.56,40,652/- through NEFT/RTGS/IMPS referred in the sale agreement dated 26-07-2021. In page No.9 of the court sale deed it is clearly mentioned that the plaintiffs have borrowed loan from SBI RACPC 3rd Doddabanasawadi branch vide loan account No.42028418527 and 41572229466 through which loan amount of Rs.1,48,39,800/- and Rs.1,80,424/- in all Rs.1,50,20,224/- paid to the account of Defendants at SBI Lingarajapuram branch in page No.10 of Court sale deed it is clearly mentioned that the plaintiffs have deposited Rs.15 Lakhs through DD No.666521dated 20-04-2024 drawn on SBI Bengaluru under RO 284/2024 dated 25-04-2024. They have also deposited Rs.6,89,124/- through DD No.000600 dated 10-06-2024 drawn on HDFC bank Nrupathunga road branch under RO No.555 dated 12-06-2024. As per the para B of page No.10 in the sale deed as per the terms of compromise dated 06-04-2023 the plaintiffs/ purchasers deposited Rs.6,89,124/- and they agreed to pay the said amount to the tenant and in that regard, tenants have already given declaration separate affidavits to the Decree-holders. Since Decree-holders agreed to pay the said amount to the tenants and tenants have already given separate declaration affidavits to the Decree-holders which is clearly noted in the registered court sale deed, the Decree-holders are entitled for Rs.6,89,124/- which they are bound to pay the said amount to the tenants as agreed in the compromise petition. Hence, IA No.3 is allowed. Office is hereby directed to pay Rs.6,89,124/- to the Decree-holders through online payment to the bank account of Decree-holders on proper identification and endorsement. For steps. Call on: 12-03-2026

hearings.judge: CCH11 VI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Notices sent against the JDRs No.1 and 2 through RPAD are returned unserved. The DHR claims that suit summons was served to the same address of the JDR No.1 and 2 in the suit and that the JDR No.1 and 2 appeared before the court in the suit and entered into compromise petition with the DHR on 06.04.2023. According to learned advocate for Decree-holder, as per the compromise decree the JDRs have received a sum of Rs.1,50,00,000/- from the Decree-holder and they are intentionally avoiding to comply with the compromise decree . Order 6 R 14 A(3) of CPC declares that for the purpose of appeal and execution, the registered address of the parties would hold good for about 2 years period after final determination of the cause or matter. In case of any change in the registered address of the party, the obligation is on the party to report to the court about change of registered address of the concerned party. The Judgment-debtor No.1 and 2 have not reported to this court either in this execution proceedings or in the original suit about the change of registered address of the Judgment-debtor No.1 and 2. It is not a case of sale of property in a public auction but sale under contemplation is in obedience to the specific performance decree which is a compromise decree. Basically having participated in the compromise petition and having received a sum of Rs.1,50,00,000/- under the compromise decree apart from receiving advance sale consideration amount of Rs.56,40,652/- from the Decree-holder under the agreement of sale, the Judgment-debtors themselves ought to have voluntarily come forward for executing sale deed in obedience to the said decree. Under the said circumstances, by noting the fact that the post man has reached the address of the Judgment-debtor and sought to tender the RPADs against them which is evidenced in the RPAD covers, it is presumed that under the above noted facts and circumstances of the case on hand, the RPADs are deemed have been served on the Judgment-debtors. The Judgment-debtors are called out, absent. Since the Judgment-debtors have failed to perform their obligation under the said decree, sale deed in respect of the suit property has to be executed through the process of the court. In this regard it would be apposite to refer to a recent judgment of the Hon\''ble Supreme Court in (2021) 6SCC 418 Rahul S Shah V/s Jinendra Kumar Gandhi and others, wherein the Honb\''le Supreme court has considered the fiat of the execution proceedings before the courts in India and ruled that the decree must be executed within 6 months from the date of presentation of petition for execution of the decree. Having considered the above noted aspects, the office is directed to verify the draft sale deed and put up note and put up the file for further proceedings on 20.04.2024.

hearings.judge: CCH44 XLIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Decree-Holder present. Case is referred to Lok-adalath. Case is called before Lok-adalath. Decree-Holder present. Counsel for Decree-Holder filed memo stating that Decree-Holder has taken possession of the property and as such execution may kindly be closed as fully satisfied. In view of memo execution petition is closed as fully satisfied.

hearings.judge: CCH44 XLIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case is advanced. Application u/s. 151 of C.P.C. filed for recall of order taking objection of Judgment-Debtor as nil along with objections. Another application u/s. 151 of C.P.C. filed for recall of delivery warrant issued. Counsel for Judgment-Debtor submits 6 months time may kindly be given to Judgment-Debtor to vacate and make alternative arrangement for residence. Counsel for Decree-Holder present and submits that the delivery warrant may be recalled if the Judgment-Debtor agrees to handover the actual possession of the property within 03.07.2024 the actually hearing date. Judgment-Debtor is not ready to handover the possession and insist that order may be passed for recall delivery warrant. Perused the order dated:24.04.2014 this court has clearly observed that as per the compromise decree which either challenged nor set aside the 2nd floor of item No.5 property is allotted to the share of the Decree-Holder. The Judgment-Debtor is in possession of the 2nd floor and as such this court has passed order for delivery of possession of 2nd floor of the item No.5 property and accordingly delivery warrant was issued. As per compromise decree property is allotted to the share of the Decree-Holder Judgment-Debtor is no right to continue in possession and as such I filed no wrong committed by this court in issuing delivery warrant. There fore no grounds are made out to recall order issuing delivery warrant. Accordingly application filed u/s. 151 of C.P.C. is hereby rejected. Counsel for Decree-Holder filed application Under Order 21 Rule 35 C.P.C. r/w/sec.151 of C.P.C. stating that police help may be given along with direction to break open the lock if any put to the premises. Judgment-Debtor present and submits that he has not objected for delivery of possession. In view of submission there is no necessary issue direction to jurisdictional to assist. However the Bailiff if permitted to break open the lock if any put to the premises by the Judgment-Debtor. Call on hearing date.

hearings.judge: CCH44 XLIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: JDR is called out, absent. No representation. Objection taken as not filed. Learned advocate for Decree-holder submits that the suit ended in compromise decree on 19.02.2020. the suit was one for partition between the plaintiffs No.1 to 3 and the Defendant. As per the compromise decree the plaintiffs No.2 and 3 got the item No.5 of the suit property to their joint share. It is for the JDR to show to the court as to what is his right to continue his possession of the said item of the suit properties. The decree holders contend that the Defendant is in possession of the 2nd floor of the item No.5 of suit properties. By virtue of decree under execution, the Decree-holders are entitled for recovery of possession of the aid 2nd floor. In a recent judgment in(2021) 6 SCC 418 Rahul S Shah V/s Jinendra Kumar Gandhi, the Hon\''ble Supreme Court has ruled regarding need for acceleration of execution proceedings so as to see that the decree holder reaps the fruits of the decree. Under the said circumstances, issue delivery warrant of delivering possession of 2nd floor of item No.5 of the suit property in favour of the Decree-holders. Call on 03.07.2024.

hearings.business_text: Case called out. Adv for DHR filed IA.No.II U/s 151 of CPC, seeking for return of original cancellation deed of JDA and original cancellation of GPA. Heard. Perused the order sheet. As per the judgment and decree passed in O.S.No.2470/2020 dated 15.06.2023, the senior Sheristedar appointed as a Court Commissioner to execute cancellation deed of JDA and cancellation of GPA. As per the office endoresment both aforesaid deeds are registered at Sub-Registrar Office in favour of DHR. hearings.business_text: Counsel for Decree-Holder absent. Counsel for Judgment-Debtor No.2 had filed order passed by joint director Co-operative society and chit fund Bengaluru in JRB/chits/appeal/24-2024-25. Accordingly I pass following: ORDER The execution petition is ordered to be closed in view of stay passed in Chit Appeal No. JRB/chits/appeal/24-2024-25 granting liberty to Decree-Holder to file fresh petition after disposal of appeal.

hearings.business_text: Counsel for JDR No.1(b) and (c) filed application Under Section 151 of CPC seeking recall of order dtd: 18.04.2024, the prayer which was already rejected by this Court. Therefore, the application is rejected. The Counsel for JDR No.1(b) and (c) filed D.D. No. 382254 dtd: 20.06.2024 towards the decreetal amount i.e., cost. Office is directed to credit the same to CCD. Counsel for JDR No.1(b) and (c) filed memo seeking adjournment on the ground that, the Writ Petition filed by the JDR No.1(b) and (c) against order dtd: 18.04.2024 is pending before the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P. NO. 16431/2024. However, the Counsel acknowledged that, there is no any stay order. The JDR has already deposited the entire decreetal amount, therefore, I am of the view of that, it is just and proper to close the petition as fully satisfied. However, considering the Writ Petition pending before Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka for consideration, office is directed not to release the amount for 15 days from the date of this order. Accordingly, petition is disposed as fully satisfied.

hearings.judge: CCH9 XXVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: On advance application filed by the JDR No.1(b) and (c), the matter is taken on board. The Counsel for JDR No.(b) and (c) filed application Section 151 of CPC to recall the order dtd: 18.04.2024, whereby this Court ordered attachment of movable properties of JDR No.1(b) and (c). On perusal of records, it appears that, the suit filed by the Plaintiff was dismissed by this Court and appeal in RFA No. 1225/2011 was allowed, consequently, suit decreed in favour of DHR, wherein Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka restrained the defendants by way of perpetual injunction from interfering with Plaintiffs peaceful possession and directed the defendants to pay the sum of Rs. 1,66,362/- towards cost incurred by the DHR to file appeal and directed to pay Rs.16,845/- towards costs incurred in trial Court. The Special Leave Petition filed by the Respondent No.2 and 3 against the judgment passed in the aforesaid RFA in Special Leave Appeal(C) No.15545/2021 was dismissed by the Hon\''ble Apex Court on 07.02.2023. Considering the above facts and age of the litigation, I am of the view of that, there is no ground made out to recall the order dtd: 18.04.2024, hence application is rejected. The JDR No.1(b) and (c) filed objections to the petition. Call on 24.06.2024.

hearings.judge: CCH16 XVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Counsel for Dhr present and filed application u/s 39 r/w Sec. 151 of CPC for transfer of decree to the court of competent jurisdiction mentioned in the body of the application. In the affidavit filed in support of present application, the GPA holder of the Dhr stated that despite the decree having being passed, the Jdrs have failed to satisfy the decree amount voluntarily thereby compelling the Dhr to initiate execution proceedings for enforcement of decree. The Jdrs have no movables and immovable property within the jurisdiction of this court to satisfy the decree. The Jdrs are voluntarily reside, carries on business in Kartik Nagar, Sowri Palyam Main Road, Coimbatore – 641028 and have immovable property within the jurisdiction of L.d. Principal District Judge, Coimbatore/District Munsif Court, Coimbatore wherefore it is prayed to issue transfer certificate and transfer the present execution proceedings to the afore mentioned court which has competent jurisdiction. The notice is not yet served on the Jdrs and it was returned unserved with remarks “Jdrs residing at Coimbatore”. As stated by the Dhr the Jdrs are presently not residing within the jurisdiction of this court, rather in the jurisdiction of the court mentioned supra. As enshrined under Sec. 39 and 40 of CPC, the court which passed a decree, on the application of the Dhr send it for execution to another court of competent jurisdiction. Where a decree is sent for execution in another state, it shall be sent to such court and executed in such manner as may be prescribed by rules in force that state. Wherefore, in view of the statements made by the Dhr and the provision of law mentioned supra, the court proceed to pass following: ORDER The application filed by the Dhr u/s 39 r/w Sec. 151 of CPC is allowed. Office is directed to transfer the decree for execution to the court of competent jurisdiction mentioned in the body of the application as provided under law.

hearings.business_text: The Decree holder and the learned counsel for the Decree holder are present. The learned counsel for the Decree holder filed I.A under Section 39 Read with Section 151 of CPC. Heard the learned counsel for the Decree holder on I.A. Perused the materials on record. The decree under Execution is money decree. The Judgment debtor is residing at Shivamogga. In the application filed by the Decree holder, it is stated that the Judgment debtor is carrying on business within jurisdiction of Shivamogga and therefore prayed to transfer the decree to Civil Court at Shivamogga. Section 39 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for transfer of decree under such circumstances. Therefore, the application is allowed and the decree under Execution is ordered to transfer to the Court of Civil Judge, Shivamogga for its execution. The office is hereby directed to send the copy of the decree to the Court of Civil Judge, Shivamogga along with certificate and copy of this order as per Rule 6 Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This petition is disposed of decree is transfer.

hearings.judge: CCH35 XXXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. It is noticed from the order sheet that, that on many occasions, this court has directed to DHR to take proper steps against Jdr on the correct address. However, despite the repeated opportunities and lapse of considerable time, the decree-holder has failed to appear and prosecute the execution petition diligently. It is relevant to refer to the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs and Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani and Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025, directed all High Courts to ensure that pending execution petitions are disposed of within a period of six months. In view of the long pendency of this execution petition, failure of the decree-holder to take any effective steps, and in light of the directions of the Hon’ble Apex Court and the High Court circular, this Court finds no reason to keep this execution petition pending any further. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non-prosecution.

Hence, Counsel for DHR is directed to provide correct address of Jdr at earliest. hearings.judge: CCH35 XXXIV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. On the last date of hearing, this court had directed to the counsel for Dhr to take further steps against Jdr However, despite the repeated and final opportunities and lapse of considerable time, the decree-holder has failed to appear and prosecute the execution petition diligently. It is relevant to refer to the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs and Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani and Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640-3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025, directed all High Courts to ensure that pending execution petitions are disposed of within a period of six months. In view of the long pendency of this execution petition, failure of the decree-holder to take any effective steps and in light of the directions of the Hon’ble Apex Court and the High Court circular, this Court finds no reason to keep this execution petition pending any further. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non-prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification.
